    #50617. Newcastle and Liverpool serve up thrilling tribute to Kevin Keegan

    📅 23 Aug 2026 • ⏱️ 32m • 📚 Deep Dive (6461 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

    Newcastle and Liverpool serve up thrilling tribute to Kevin Keegan

    📅 23 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 32 min read (6461 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~32 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that it had to end that way, didn’t it?
    • Newcastle versus Liverpool became the Premier League’s most dramatic fixture when Kevin Keegan was manager here and, on the afternoon they flocked to the “cathedral on the hill” to pay tribute to the late, great superstar, we were treated to a contest that was in keeping with his narrative.
    • Liverpool operating with the discipline of a basketball team undoubtedly helped, and we can examine those gaping chasms soon enough, but the poignancy of seeing Matthias Jaissle looking as bereft as Keegan at Anfield 30 years ago at the final whistle was impossible to ignore.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that it had to end that way, didn’t it? A last-minute goal, a sense of what might have been and a helter-skelter contest that will take days to decipher.

    Newcastle versus Liverpool became the Premier League’s most dramatic fixture when Kevin Keegan was manager here and, on the afternoon they flocked to the “cathedral on the hill” to pay tribute to the late, great superstar, we were treated to a contest that was in keeping with his narrative.

    Liverpool operating with the discipline of a basketball team undoubtedly helped, and we can examine those gaping chasms soon enough, but the poignancy of seeing Matthias Jaissle looking as bereft as Keegan at Anfield 30 years ago at the final whistle was impossible to ignore.

    Really, the German’s first match in charge of Newcastle should have ended with three points. His team are a work in progress – rich in youthful exuberance though prone to lapses – but how they fought, ran and worked to give the locals the result they wanted.

    Industry observers note that they were almost at the finish line, seconds away from beating Liverpool here for the first time since December 2015, but then Lewis Hall ran into Victor Muñoz, sending the Spanish substitute sprawling, and Stuart Attwell pointed to the penalty spot. Dominik Szoboszlai inflicted maximum damage.

    Sources indicate that dominik Szoboszlai equalises from the spot in the 99th minute! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/0Ag9WitqHt.

    “I have clear thoughts,” Jaissle noted quietly, as he was asked to reflect on the day-wrecking decision. “I guess you call it a soft penalty here. If you give it, you need to give a lot during this match and a lot during the season. I don’t know if it that is good for football.”.

    Here was the third time in four seasons Liverpool had scored in injury time in front of the Leazes Stand, after Darwin Núñez (2023) and Rio Ngumoha (2025), and their eighth goal beyond the 90th minute in collisions with Newcastle is a Premier League record against the same opponents.

    Sources indicate that no wonder he was stunned. Jaissle had spent idle moments in the build-up thinking about what might happen if Newcastle scored an early goal and, much to his delight, fantasy became reality in the most thrilling fashion. On this emotional afternoon, it was fitting the hosts scored first.

    Sources indicate that one of Keegan’s great early wins as Newcastle manager was in November 1993, when his team blew away Liverpool in the snow and Andy Cole scored a first-half hat-trick. His first goal that day came after five minutes and, by happy coincidence, the clock stopped at that moment for Anthony Elanga, too.

    How Liverpool went from having a chance of their own to conceding 20 seconds later is something Andoni Iraola will have to address swiftly, but that is what happened: Ryan Gravenberch should have shot, instead he passed and Amar Dedic intervened, his interception finding Will Osula.

    Off Osula galloped, Liverpool’s defenders looking leaden-footed as they gave pursuit, and he ushered Elanga into open space. Once he was in the clear, he was not for catching and his shot was perfectly placed beyond Alisson Becker.

    Industry observers note that an electric start! Anthony Elanga gives Newcastle the lead inside 5 minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/8DYYFJ9i6F.

    In a recent development, as Elanga was mobbed, the recriminations started. Fingers pointed at each other, Iraola spun around in dismay. Liverpool were easy to play against last season – Iraola’s Bournemouth had scored two identical goals against them on the opening day 12 months ago – and old habits die hard.

    It has been revealed that “We should finish the play,” Iraola conceded. “We created a great chance. We are on the edge of the box and have a clear opening to shoot and we decide not to. We don’t finish it properly and then you have to give credit to Elanga, who wins the race.”.

    According to recent reports, what could Liverpool offer in response? The answer before the interval was nothing, other than a shot from Florian Wirtz that was well saved by Lukas Hornicek. The first half was wretched and it was difficult to see what had changed from the final throes of Arne Slot.

    This, to be clear, is no criticism of Iraola, more a spotlight on players who need to step up. They did that momentarily in the second period, when Cody Gakpo equalised. He was afforded too much time by Newcastle’s defence but, still, his finish from 20 yards was super, zipping beyond Hornicek.

    Industry observers note that cody Gakpo with a fine finish to equalise for Liverpool! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/cfDQWbES2v.

    But parity was secured for less than two minutes before Newcastle scored a near-carbon-copy second goal, another counter-attack – this was one led by the outstanding Yoane Wissa – ending with substitute Joe Willock finding a corner of Alisson’s net. Again the inquests followed.

    Recent findings suggest that "Wow!"Joe Willock restores Newcastle's advantage almost instantly with an exceptional finish! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/8IKPUgqapK.

    It is fitting that Newcastle United vs Liverpool is a Premier League opening weekend fixture following the death of Kevin Keegan at the age of 75 last month.

Central midfield has not been replenished; they need a Mohamed Salah replacement, and their strength at full-back is questionable.     #50595. Tyler Herro scores 50, officials miss late out-of-bounds call on Joel Embiid in 76ers' 132-129 win over Bucks

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (442 w)
    📖 Baca
    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Yahoo ↗ Open Full Page

    Tyler Herro scores 50, officials miss late out-of-bounds call on Joel Embiid in 76ers' 132-129 win over Bucks

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (442 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Tyler Herro scored a career-high 50 points Saturday, but that wasn't enough for the Milwaukee Bucks to get their second win of the season in a 132-129 defeat to the Philadelphia 76ers.
    • Milwaukee was deprived of an opportunity to take the lead in the closing seconds when officials missed Joel Embiid stepping out of bounds.
    • Sources indicate that rookie Brayden Burries hit a corner 3-pointer for the Bucks to cut the Sixers' lead to 130-129.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Tyler Herro scored a career-high 50 points Saturday, but that wasn't enough for the Milwaukee Bucks to get their second win of the season in a 132-129 defeat to the Philadelphia 76ers.

    Milwaukee was deprived of an opportunity to take the lead in the closing seconds when officials missed Joel Embiid stepping out of bounds.

    Sources indicate that rookie Brayden Burries hit a corner 3-pointer for the Bucks to cut the Sixers' lead to 130-129. After a timeout, LeBron James threw an inbounds pass to Embiid, who attempted to dribble out the clock near the Milwaukee basket. Embiid stepped out of bounds at the baseline with his left foot, but the officials did not call the turnover and Herro was forced to foul.

    The Bucks could not challenge the non-call because they were out of replay challenges.

    Embiid made his two free throws to put Philadelphia ahead by 3, but the Bucks still had 1.5 seconds remaining to try for a tying basket.

    It has been revealed that herro received the inbounds pass from Kyle Kuzma at the top of the arc and took one dribble to break free from VJ Edgecombe. Shooting from the right elbow, Herro's 3-pointer went in. However, the shot left his hand after the buzzer.

    It has been revealed that the eighth-year guard shot 15 for 23 from the floor, including 7 of 13 on 3-pointers. Herro also hit all 11 of his free throws, adding 11 rebounds and seven assists. Burries finished with 26 points off the bench with 8 rebounds and four assists. Kuzma was the third Bucks player to reach double figures, scoring 12 with five boards.

    Herro's previous career-high was 41 points, reached in a December 2022 win over the Houston Rockets while he was with the Miami Heat.

    It has been revealed that milwaukee lost its 13th consecutive game to drop to 1-16 on the season, the worst mark in the NBA. The Bucks' only win came nearly a month ago on Oct. 26, a 110-102 victory over the Indiana Pacers. Up next for them is the Toronto Raptors (6-10) at home on Monday.

    Embiid led the Sixers with 26 points, nearly registering a triple-double with 17 rebounds and nine assists. James added 21 points with 6 boards, 6 assists and 3 steals. Seven Philadelphia players scored in double figures, with Anfernee Simons getting 18 off the bench and Tyrese Maxey tallying 17 points.

    The 76ers improved to 14-3 with the win, tying the Los Angeles Lakers for the NBA's top record. Philadelphia has won five consecutive games and next faces the Portland Trail Blazers (10-5) on Monday.

    Palmer and Rogers show promise of star double act for Chelsea

    📅 25 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 28 min read (5519 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~28 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The stirring of what might yet be a great partnership between Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, although it will need to be, given some of the chaos that endures at Chelsea.
    • It has been revealed that this was a Premier League game played at a furious pace, and the two former Real Madrid team-mates in charge of the sides will not have seen much of the control all coaches seek.
    • In a recent development, that was chiefly the fault of Robert Sánchez, who was embraced afterwards by Alonso, having demonstrated just how damaging a shaky goalkeeper can be to any serious team.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The stirring of what might yet be a great partnership between Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, although it will need to be, given some of the chaos that endures at Chelsea.

    It has been revealed that this was a Premier League game played at a furious pace, and the two former Real Madrid team-mates in charge of the sides will not have seen much of the control all coaches seek. Xabi Alonso’s team eventually won with a goal from each of his attacking triumvirate of Rogers, Palmer and João Pedro – and at times it will have been painful for the new Chelsea manager.

    In a recent development, that was chiefly the fault of Robert Sánchez, who was embraced afterwards by Alonso, having demonstrated just how damaging a shaky goalkeeper can be to any serious team. Álvaro Arbeloa’s Fulham had their moments – and the best ones were granted to them by Sánchez. At a club that is such a restless trader of footballers, it feels remarkable that Sánchez has endured for so long.

    According to recent reports, alonso played down the significance of Sánchez’s errors, although he cannot seriously be considering sticking to his mantra of “relax and carry on”. That was, he said, his response to the first-half Sánchez mistake that let in Josh King’s shot for Fulham’s first goal. Sánchez could have done a lot better with Gonzalo García’s goal after the break.

    Fulham have equalised against Chelsea thanks to Josh King's low strike 💥 pic.twitter.com/WCLKB7XqeE.

    Gonzalo Garcia has scored on his Premier League debut after Robert Sanchez spilled Castagne's shot 🤯 pic.twitter.com/BmP6eqwkuN.

    Chelsea have a lot of faith that Mike Penders, the 21-year-old Belgian on the bench for this game, will be their first-choice goalkeeper eventually. The situation seems rather more urgent and with Penders likely to feature against Luton Town on Thursday night in the Carabao Cup it would appear a big decision is looming for Alonso.

    According to recent reports, in terms of the Palmer-Rogers axis, this was very promising, although there was no doubting the senior figure in this. Palmer’s ball set João Pedro free in the first minute, the Brazilian lifting a well-judged nudge over Bernd Leno.

    "A flying start under Xabi Alonso!" Chelsea lead against Fulham after just 31 seconds 🤯 pic.twitter.com/LrkYxOReFB.

    It was Palmer who was crucial to the second for Rogers, made by Maxence Lacroix on his debut. Palmer stroked in the third on 49 minutes with the easy confidence of a man in form.

    A goal for Morgan Rogers on his Chelsea debut! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/hphe8y077v.

    According to recent reports, "Cole Palmer back to his best!"Palmer has scored to double Chelsea's lead! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/zo6e0Vdcgq.

    Recent findings suggest that “I am very happy for Cole,” Alonso said. “I have really enjoyed seeing him play with the dynamism and the freedom and the responsibility... when Cole feels this way we have a better team and a better Cole.”.

    Industry observers note that palmer makes it look very easy in this form, capable of switching the direction of play a beat before anyone else spots the opportunity. He and his old Manchester City academy friend Rogers came off before the end, Palmer having demonstrated some discomfort chasing a ball. Asked afterwards how ready he felt, Palmer responded in kind. “Did you not watch the game? I’m only joking, I’m ready... it was a difficult season with injuries and whatnot, but through the summer and since I’ve been back I’ve worked extra hard.”.

    If there was an attacker to compare with him on the other side it was King, who looks even better. The 19-year-old was way ahead of Arbeloa’s two young Real Madrid imports. García toiled away and took his chance, but César Palacios struggled for any impact in a position tucked in on the left. Oscar Bobb and King gave Fulham some edge but the concern, as ever, will be where Fulham get their goals.

    Sources indicate that arbeloa pushed his full-backs high and encouraged Sander Berge to drop deep to get on the ball in the first passing phase. The Norwegian delayed too long in challenging João Pedro for Chelsea’s third – backing off and allowing Palmer to overlap to receive the pass.

    Sources indicate that sánchez had not been the only concern for Chelsea. Back in the team, Levi Colwill misjudged a challenge on King in the first half and was relieved that the card was only yellow. Roméo Lavia took a wild swing at Calvin Bassey and was also booked. Moisés Caicedo was not fit to play. Enzo Fernández was on the bench and would come on in the second half to the kind of reception from opposition fans to which he will quickly become familiar.

    In a recent development, there was a grin from the Argentine at those who berated him from the home stands when he returned at half-time. Fernández worked hard to transmit a general sense that the abuse did not land, although he will be relieved that the Chelsea fans were supportive. His future still feels very much in play.

    Sources indicate that it was Palmer’s subtle ball through that gave João Pedro the chance with 32 seconds of the game played. The ball came forward immediately from Lacroix’s firm header from defence. The Frenchman delivered a very accomplished assist for Rogers’s first-half goal. Before that King had equalised. There was an exchange with Timothy Castagne, and King looked up just inside the box and decided to have a swing at it. Sánchez was close enough to grasp the ball and somehow failed to do so.

    It has been revealed that sánchez would later push a Castagne shot in the direction of García, who stooped and nodded the ball over the goalkeeper after Palmer had scored Chelsea’s third. This second error was unfortunate, but it is the kind of thing that happens to a goalkeeper as erratic as the one for whom Chelsea’s hierarchy seem to have such patience.

    Sources indicate that “We concede goals in the first minute, the end of the first half and the beginning of the second half and there are not worse moments to concede. But we showed character and personality and I am very proud of how my players responded. We deserved a little bit more but football is not about what you deserve, it is about what you take. If you lose against a team like Chelsea they [should] have to do a little bit more. For me, they are easy goals for them and mistakes we cannot make. We need to improve and be more ready in the first minute, that is for sure.

    “We are on our way and we will keep improving. The first thing I want to see is a competitive team. We were tonight, we tried our best and tried to play our football against a team like Chelsea, which is not easy. I believe in them and I believe in young players. I think they have the energy and ambition I want and they fit in the way I play. Josh King is absolutely amazing. I am really happy with him. Gonzalo [Garcia] scored and Cesar [Palacios] did well. I think they need a bit more time but they are doing great and making an impact already.”.

    "We need to help them, not to rely everything on them" Xabi Alonso speaking about Chelsea's 'special' front three 🔵 pic.twitter.com/JnSBoNexF4.

    "Arsenal DON'T win the league if they have Ramsdale and not Raya" 🧤@Carra23 and @GNev2 think that upgrading the goalkeeper position could be the 'last piece' for Chelsea 🧩 pic.twitter.com/UBzMCFmxpp.

    "You can see in his eyes, he's ready to prove people wrong""Best player on the pitch by a mile" 👏Morgan Rogers reacts to his debut and the performance of Cole Palmer pic.twitter.com/M7JKk1MQ8U.

    Recent findings suggest that "How ready are you?""Did you not watch the game?" 😅Cole Palmer says he is 'hungry' and ready to get back to his best! pic.twitter.com/xpg5zJl9k0.

    It has been revealed that 2 - Cole Palmer tonight vs Fulham:1 goal1 assist5 dribbles completed5 shots3 chances created7 ball recoveries10 duels wonHe was only the second player on record since 2006-07 to record all of these numbers in a Premier League game.Cold. pic.twitter.com/uW4YPeHNnD.

    “There were things to really like. On paper, that front three [for Chelsea] is sensational. It really is. It looked it in the game. I think Joao Pedro is fantastic. [Morgan] Rogers’ first game, what a start. But when you think of him, [Cole] Palmer and Pedro; that is as good as anything in the Premier League right now.

    Sources indicate that “But I do think concerns defensively. They conceded a couple of goals and you look at the goalkeeper. They have to sort the goalkeeper problem out because it is going to come back to haunt them this season, as it did tonight.”.

    August 27: Fulham vs AFC Wimbledon (League Cup)August 30: Sunderland vs Fulham (Premier League)September 5: Fulham vs Crystal Palace (Premier League)September 12: Liverpool vs Fulham (Premier League)September 20: Fulham vs Manchester United (Premier League).

    Sources indicate that “The attacking play, Cole Palmer was sensational. If you talk about Cole Palmer getting back to his best you have got a £120m-£125m player there. [Morgan] Rogers getting a goal. Those two being electric with Joao Pedro up front. The front three were brilliant tonight. One of the best things I have seen this weekend.

    “They have added an experience player at centre-back, centre midfield and centre forward. I do not know if Emi Martinez is available or not but someone like that needs to come in at Chelsea, because that will undermine everything they do. The positives for Fulham came from the encouragement [Robert] Sanchez gave them with the goals. The goals were both mistakes. It is a problem.”.

    Possession: Fulham 61%-39% ChelseaShots: 14-18Shots on target: 6-6Corners: 6-4Touches in opposition box: 24-38.

    Sources indicate that the final whistle is blown at Craven Cottage and Chelsea hold on to win 3-2 to give Xabi Alonso a win in his first game in charge. Alvaro Arbeloa’s first game as Fulham boss ends in defeat. An absorbing west London derby.

    Garcia throws himself to the ground as Sessegnon sends in a cross but that is never going to be a penalty.

    In a recent development, will there be one more chance for Fulham to try and find an equaliser? Time is running out for the hosts.

    According to recent reports, pedro has the ball in the back of the Fulham net but Quenda was offside in the build-up. A quick VAR check proves so.

    There will be four added minutes.

    Surely there is another goal in this one? It is a surprise there has not been since Garcia got a goal back for Fulham.

    The latest booking of the game goes the way of Castagne, who cynically trips Colwill.

    Sessegnon is played in down the left channel and flicks it past Acheampong inside the Chelsea penalty area. Sessegnon gets his shot away from a narrow angle and it is straight at Sanchez.

    Industry observers note that palmer looks like he might have cramp in his calf and is going to be replaced by Estevao. Quenda also comes on for Chelsea, coming on for Rogers.

    Fulham make an attacking alteration as Muniz replaces Robinson.

    According to recent reports, that is a huge, huge chance for Fulham to equalise. Robinson is played in behind the Chelsea defence with a long ball in behind and Sanchez is in no-man’s land out of his goal. Robinson just has to lift it over Sanchez from the edge of the box but his effort goes wide. Fulham should be on level terms.

    Industry observers note that fulham fans think they are about to be awarded a free-kick right outside the box but instead the free-kick goes the other way. It was a clear dive from Bassey, who is rightly booked for simulation.

    Recent findings suggest that james is the third Chelsea player into the book for cynically pulling King back. James then has the cheek to wag his finger at King, as if it was not a foul, yet it was a clear booking. James had to be careful there as some referees may not have taken too kindly to that.

    Double change for Fulham as Kevin and Sessegnon are brought on.

    Sources indicate that that would have been a great goal from King. He has already scored once and is inches away from his second. He receives a pass on the turn from Robinson and drives towards the Chelsea box. He then cuts inside onto his right, beating Lacroix with ease, and nearly beats Sanchez at his near post but his shot goes inches wide.

    This is a very open, end-to-end game and you would fully expect more goals in this one. I would be very surprised if this one ended 3-2. Both defences are looking leaky.

    Fulham are going to make their substitution of the night as Charles comes on for his debut having signed from Southampton, replacing Bobb.

    Enzo is being booed a lot by the home fans every time he touches the ball.

    It has been revealed that chelsea are the first to turn to their bench. Enzo is coming on and is met by a lot of boos, mostly though from the home fans as the majority of the travelling Chelsea fans are applauding him. Chavarria is also on to make his Chelsea debut. Hato and Lavia head off.

    There is a latest rule being implemented. Hato takes far too long over a throw-in and Fulham are therefore awarded the throw-in instead.

    Recent findings suggest that when Palmer put Chelsea 3-1 up, the visitors looked in control of this match. Fast forward five minutes and the momentum has completely switched around. What an absorbing opening Monday night of the season!

    Sources indicate that the Fulham debutant gives them life and this game is not over. Castagne is found making a run in behind and cuts back inside onto his left inside the Chelsea penalty area. His shot is straight at Sanchez, who can only parry it straight into the path of Garcia, who heads into the ground and the ball bounces over Sanchez into the Chelsea net. Another poor piece of goalkeeping from Sanchez.

    Gonzalo Garcia has scored on his Premier League debut after Robert Sanchez spilled Castagne's shot 🤯 pic.twitter.com/BmP6eqwkuN.

    All members of Chelsea’s starting front three have got on the scoresheet tonight and Palmer also has an assist to his name.

    Chelsea come close to a fourth as Hato squares it for Rogers inside the Fulham box but Robinson nips in just in front to clear.

    It has been revealed that he came close to scoring moments ago and now he does get on the scoresheet. Pedro gets onto the end of a flicked-on header by Rogers near halfway and drives into the Fulham half. As he gets to the Fulham penalty area, he waits for the overlapping run of Palmer and times the pass just right. Palmer, from a narrow angle, puts it between Leno’s legs and into the far corner.

    "Cole Palmer back to his best!"Palmer has scored to double Chelsea's lead! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/zo6e0Vdcgq.

    Palmer does brilliantly down Chelsea’s right to skip past a number of defenders and moves into the Fulham penalty area. He opens up his body and curls one towards the far corner. He is adamant that there is a deflection but a goal kick is given. Replays show Palmer may have had a point.

    We are back under way at Craven Cottage.

    Nottingham Forest are ramping up their pursuit of Chelsea’s Liam Delap as Oliver Glasner eyes two major signings before the window closes.

    Forest are in talks with Chelsea over a potential loan deal for the forward after he was made available at Stamford Bridge and not included in their opening-day squad against Fulham.

    Negotiations are ongoing, but Delap fits the profile of striker Forest are prioritising and is a long-term target for both the club and Glasner from his spell at Crystal Palace.

    Possession: Fulham 60%-40% ChelseaShots: 7-13Shots on target: 2-5Corners: 4-3Touches in opposition box: 16-18.

    An absorbing first half at Craven Cottage is brought to a close and Chelsea take a 2-1 lead into the break. Pedro put them ahead inside the first minute before King equalised for Fulham. However Rogers, on his Chelsea debut, put the visitors back in front not long before half-time.

    There will be two added minutes at the end of this first half.

    According to recent reports, palmer, who has run the show for Chelsea in this first half, is inches away from putting the visitors 3-1 up. Both sides have been guilty of giving the ball away in dangerous areas and Fulham do so on this occasion. Palmer then curls an effort from the edge of the box but his shot goes just wide of the far post.

    In a recent development, the British record transfer puts Chelsea back in front on his official debut. It stems from great play from centre-back Lacroix, who finds himself in an advanced position and receives a pass from Palmer on the right side of the box. Lacroix cuts it across to Rogers, who makes no mistake from 12 yards out. Assist and goal both coming from upcoming signings.

    A goal for Morgan Rogers on his Chelsea debut! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/hphe8y077v.

    Fulham fail to clear a cross from James into their box and Hato’s header falls at the feet of Lavia, whose shot from close range is saved by Leno.

    In a recent development, is Colwill lucky to still be on the pitch? The ball is played in behind the Chelsea defence and Colwill appeared to throw his arm across King but no foul is given. That could so easily have been given as a free-kick and a second yellow card.

    Recent findings suggest that rogers drives towards the Fulham box and cuts inside onto his right foot. His effort is blocked by Cuenca before James’ first-time shot is straight at Leno.

    According to recent reports, chelsea are inches from going back in front. It stems from great work from Palmer, who drives down Chelsea’s right. His cross from the right side of the box picks out Pedro near the penalty spot. The Brazilian volleys it first time but his effort goes just wide.

    It has been revealed that fulham are on top at the moment and Chelsea are lucky shaky as they are under the cosh inside their own box. King is playing really well, finding pockets of space down Fulham’s right and looking a real threat.

    Fulham are back on level terms but it is really poor goalkeeping from Sanchez. King, who had just threatened down Fulham’s right, receives a pass from Castagne on the right touchline and takes a touch into the Chelsea box. King then fires his shot away at the near post and gets plenty of power on it but there is no way Sanchez should be beaten. He is beaten and Fulham equalise. Good strike from King but terrible keeping from Sanchez.

    Fulham have equalised against Chelsea thanks to Josh King's low strike 💥 pic.twitter.com/WCLKB7XqeE.

    Recent findings suggest that chelsea haven’t spent all that money on Rogers for his defending, but Alonso won’t have liked the way he let Josh King to run past him to collect the ball and smash Fulham level. Rogers switched off there.

    King does brilliantly to drive down Fulham’s right and flashes a dangerous ball across the six-yard box but none of his teammates are on hand to meet the cross.

    Fulham are flirting with danger in and around their box and are a touch fortunate not to concede a second goal.

    Down the other end, King is urged to shoot from outside the box and he obliges. It looks like it should be a fairly routine save for Sanchez but the Chelsea keeper looks uncomfortable and pushes it behind for a corner. The delivery comes to the near post and King, who lays it off the edge of the box. It comes to Palacios, who cannot guide his effort on target.

    In a recent development, chelsea started this game well but have lost control and are asking for trouble. The latest example sees Sanchez take too long to clear and he accidentally allows the ball to go out before clearing to gift Fulham a corner. Bobb’s delivery is headed away at the near post by James.

    Sources indicate that that is strong one-vs-one defending from Bassey. Palmer lifts the ball over the top to pick out the run of Pedro, who is dispossessed inside the Fulham box by Bassey.

    Industry observers note that moments later, Lavia flies into a reckless challenge on Bassey and is booked. Lavia looks stunned at that decision but he is perhaps on the fortunate side that VAR did not advise the referee to have a further look at that on the screen. Lavia was out of control and could have easily been in more trouble. Two Chelsea players already into the book and were a little bit lucky.

    Palmer had just one Premier League assist to his name throughout last season and has already matched that tally tonight on the opening weekend.

    In a recent development, colwill is in trouble. Could Chelsea go down to 10 men early? He loses possession poorly inside his own half and then resorts to hacking Bobb down with a nasty challenge. Was Colwill the last man and could Bobb have gone racing in on goal? Colwill is booked and is perhaps a touch fortunate, although what saved him is that you perhaps could not definitively say that it was a denial of a goal-scoring opportunity.

    How do Alvaro Arbeloa and his Fulham side react now they are a goal down early?

    In a recent development, with their first attack of the Xabi Alonso era, Chelsea hit the front inside the opening minute of this west London derby. Lacroix’s header from halfway finds Palmer, who plays it into the path of Pedro. The Brazilian, fresh from signing a newly introduced deal at the club, takes it in his stride and, from inside the Fulham penalty area, lifts it over Leno and into the far corner. A fine finish from Pedro and Alonso has the perfect start.

    "A flying start under Xabi Alonso!" Chelsea lead against Fulham after just 31 seconds 🤯 pic.twitter.com/LrkYxOReFB.

    Could Joao Pedro be the man to finally lift the curse of the number nine shirt at Chelsea? Liam Delap tried and failed last season. Pedro has taken it this term and has started like a train with that early goal. Pedro has also been prolific in pre-season and has been widely tipped to be one of the Premier League’s top scorers.

    Before we get going, we take a moment to remember the great Kevin Keegan, who managed Fulham in the late 1990s.

    We are under way at Craven Cottage in the final game on this opening weekend of the latest Premier League season.

    Alvaro Arbeloa is out on the pitch for the first time in the Premier League. A friendly if not rapturous welcome from the home fans. He’s rolled his sleeves up and he’s ready to go - literally, his skinny fit jacket has sleeves rolled up tight. It looks quite uncomfortable.

    Industry observers note that it might be a newly introduced season and a new manager, but Chelsea are still doing their pre-match huddle. Fortunately, it was nowhere near the referee or the centre circle. It seemed to be captain Reece James doing all the talking.

    According to recent reports, both sides emerge from the tunnel at Craven Cottage and we are moments away from kick-off in this west London derby. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up tonight:.

    Fulham: Leno; Castagne, Cuenca, Bassey, Robinson, King, Berge, Iwobi; Bobb, Garcia, Palacios.Substitutes: Lecomte, De Gougerolles, Tete, Reed, Charles, Sessegnon, Kevin, Smith Rowe, Muniz.

    Chelsea: Sanchez; Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill; Gusto, Lavia, James, Hato; Palmer, Pedro, Rogers.Substitutes: Penders, Chavarria, Barco, Enzo, Neto, Gittens, Estevao, Welbeck, Quenda.

    Sources indicate that the boos for Fernandez from the Fulham fans got a lot louder when the players stepped on the pitch. Some people chanted something rather nasty beginning with ‘w’ as well.

    In a recent development, there were a few boos from the Fulham fans when Enzo Fernandez’s name was read out ahead of kick-off. Clearly the England fans at Craven Cottage haven’t forgotten what happened against Argentina. Fernandez was booed by some Chelsea supporters in pre-season, but there were no loud jeers from the away end during the team announcements.

    “During the week they had a few setbacks. With Moises [Caicedo], and with any [player], we do not want to take too much risk. They were not ready to play tonight. We need to go week-by-week but for tonight they were not ready.”.

    It has been revealed that chelsea certainly have an army of staff. I just counted 13 staff members helping the players through their warm-up. One of them is the new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee, who is carrying around a clipboard, presumably with all his set-piece tricks on it. Culture guru Willi Isa is also out there, as is former interim manager Calum McFarlane.

    "The day to day culture that we want to build, they will play an crucial role" 📈Xabi Alonso explains his choice to join Chelsea and the importance of signings like Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0koZ7ZyYYx.

    Sources indicate that chelsea’s £117m man Morgan Rogers has just run out for his warm up ahead of his competitive debut for the club. He’s kept in close contact with his best mate Cole Palmer, going through a few passing drills and doing a few keepy-ups. He looks relaxed so far.

    "You NEED goals if you want to win games" ⚽️Fresh Fulham head coach Alvaro Arbeloa speaks about the losses of Harry Wilson and Raul Jimenez and the addition of Gonzalo Garcia 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/tbBujmljxm.

    INS:Marco Palestra ⇠ Atalanta, £42mGeovany Quenda ⇠ Sporting, £42mMorgan Rogers ⇠ Aston Villa, £117mMaxence Lacroix ⇠ Crystal Palace, £51mDanny Welbeck ⇠ Brighton, UndisclosedJordan Henderson ⇠ Brentford, FreeValentin Barco ⇠ Strasbourg, UndisclosedPep Chavarria ⇠ Rayo Vallecano, £16m.

    OUTS:Andrey Santos ⇢ Manchester United, £50mMarc Cucurella ⇢ Real Madrid, £50mTyrique George ⇢ Everton, £24mAlejandro Garnacho ⇢ Aston Villa, LoanTrevoh Chalobah ⇢ Como, £30mFilip Jorgensen ⇢ Strasbourg, LoanDastan Satpaev ⇢ Burnley, LoanBenoit Badiashile ⇢ Napoli, Loan.

    "There is a LOT of risk associated with Fulham" 👀Gary Neville thinks that it could be a tough season ahead for the Cottagers 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/0Lpa4zxPti.

    INS:Gonzalo Garcia ⇠ Real Madrid, £32mShea Charles ⇠ Southampton, £30mCesar Palacios ⇠ Real Madrid, £10mJonah Kusi-Asare ⇠ Bayern Munich, £5m.

    OUTS:Sasa Lukic ⇢ Ipswich, £9mIssa Diop ⇢ Ipswich, £8mHarry Wilson ⇢ Leeds, FreeRaul Jimenez ⇢ Wolves, Free.

    "Chelsea have done really well to get a manager of that calibre" 🙌@Carra23 explains why he is expecting Chelsea to do well this season 🔵Watch MNF live: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/qQjvutu9Hz.

    The most interesting piece of Chelsea team news is that there is no Enzo Fernandez in the starting line-up, despite the surprise absence of Moises Caicedo. Instead, Romeo Lavia will partner Reece James in the centre of midfield, with Caicedo presumably injured. There is still an expectation that Manchester City will bid for Fernandez before the transfer window shuts, but the Argentine is on the substitutes’ bench. As expected, there is no place in the Chelsea squad for Nico Jackson and Liam Delap, both of whom have not travelled and are expected to leave Stamford Bridge. Aston Villa remain favourites to land Jackson, although Atletico Madrid have been showing an interest. Nottingham Forest are leading the race for Delap.

    It has been revealed that alvaro Arbeloa hands full debuts to Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios, who have both joined from Real Madrid. Shea Charles is on the bench ahead of his potential Fulham debut.

    Fulham: Leno; Castagne, Cuenca, Bassey, Robinson, King, Berge, Iwobi; Bobb, Garcia, Palacios.Substitutes: Lecomte, De Gougerolles, Tete, Reed, Charles, Sessegnon, Kevin, Smith Rowe, Muniz.

    Industry observers note that morgan Rogers and Maxence Lacroix make their full Chelsea debuts this evening. Fellow latest signings Danny Welbeck, Valentin Barco, Pep Chavarria and Geovany Quenda are on the bench, as is Enzo Fernandez, who has been linked with a move away. Moises Caicedo is not in the matchday squad.

    Chelsea: Sanchez; Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill; Gusto, Lavia, James, Hato; Palmer, Pedro, Rogers.Substitutes: Penders, Chavarria, Barco, Enzo, Neto, Gittens, Estevao, Welbeck, Quenda.

    According to recent reports, no more excuses. No more jam tomorrow. It is time for Chelsea to fight for the Premier League title this season. Anything else should be deemed a disappointment.

    This is Chelsea version 3.0 under BlueCo, who bought the club four years ago. First there was Todd Boehly’s trolley dash, then came Behdad Eghbali’s youth club. This summer the focus has been on being Premier League-ready.

    Off the pitch, the timing might be right for Boehly to be discussing the sale of his shares to Eghbali’s Clearlake Capital. But on it, Chelsea look better equipped to re-enter the title conversation than at any point in the BlueCo era.

    Saturday:Hull 2 Manchester United 0Everton 2 Crystal Palace 0Ipswich 2 Sunderland 1Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds 1Brentford 3 Tottenham 0.

    Sunday:Manchester City 2 Bournemouth 1Brighton 4 Aston Villa 0Newcastle 2 Liverpool 2.

    Let's get it.#CFC | #FULCHE pic.twitter.com/G2M8LknNgV.

    Monday Night Fulham. ⚪️ pic.twitter.com/Oxuni9yiez.

    Two former Liverpool, Real Madrid and Spain teammates go head-to-head in the dugouts at Craven Cottage as Fulham host Chelsea in a west London derby to round out the opening weekend of the latest Premier League season. Alvaro Arbeloa and Xabi Alonso were teammates at Liverpool, Real Madrid and Spain and both had stints as Real Madrid manager last season but have new homes in London. Arbeloa has replaced Marco Silva, who is now at Benfica, whilst Alonso is Liam Rosenior’s permanent replacement. This is the first time a manager’s Premier League debut has come against someone he also played alongside in the competition.

    In a recent development, “I know Alonso well because I have watched so many games of his teams,” Arbeloa said. “We have to be ready, and if we want to beat them we will have to play very well. I spoke to Xabi a few days ago. But not about football; both of our families are coming to London, and we are very good friends, until Monday night [tonight]. We will be there on the touchline, so close for 90 minutes, and we will give everything for our clubs. For those 90 minutes, we are not friends.”.

    Arbeloa has gone back to his former club to add a couple of players in the shape of Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios. The opening weekend has not served Fulham well of late; they have won just one of their last six Premier League opening weekend fixtures. They concluded their pre-season with a 1-0 win over Stuttgart.

    Chelsea have been very active in the transfer market this summer, breaking the British transfer record to sign Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa as well as adding experience through the likes of Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck, whilst the likes of Marc Cucurella, Andrey Santos and Trevoh Chalobah have moved on. They finished off their pre-season with a 3-1 victory over Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge just over a week ago.

    It has been revealed that “We feel ready,” Alonso noted. “We have prepared the whole pre-season with some players from the first day, other ones coming later, but the desire, the ambition, the hunger to start the Premier League is already in the building each training [session] and we are looking forward to it.”.

    Enzo Fernandez has been strongly linked with a move away this summer, with Manchester City’s interest well-known.

    “Enzo is a Chelsea player,” Alonso added. “He is a top, top player. He is training really well since he started 10 days ago with the team, very integrated. We are happy with him and he is getting ready for Monday. He is training really well, good attitude and that is what we want. He is trying his best to prepare for the kick-off of the Premier League.”.

    Sources indicate that these sides finished on the same number of points (52) last season, with Chelsea finishing ahead on goal difference. It was one win apiece for each club in the two Premier League meetings last season. Nearly a year ago, Chelsea won 2-0 at Stamford Bridge whilst Fulham won 2-1 in this fixture at Craven Cottage back in January. Chelsea have won six of the past eight Premier League meetings at Craven Cottage.

    #50557. Glasner made to wait for first win as Trafford thwarts Forest

    📅 25 Aug 2026 • ⏱️ 21m • 📚 Deep Dive (4132 w)
    📖 Baca
    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

    Glasner made to wait for first win as Trafford thwarts Forest

    📅 25 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 21 min read (4132 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • James Trafford became the record signing for a British goalkeeper this summer and he is already proving invaluable for Leeds United.
    • Signed from Manchester City for an initial £40m in August, Trafford has made an outstanding start and frustrated Nottingham Forest twice in four days.
    • The England international secured his second successive clean sheet in this City Ground sequel to underline why Leeds moved to eclipse the previous record for Jordan Pickford.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    James Trafford became the record signing for a British goalkeeper this summer and he is already proving invaluable for Leeds United.

    Signed from Manchester City for an initial £40m in August, Trafford has made an outstanding start and frustrated Nottingham Forest twice in four days.

    The England international secured his second successive clean sheet in this City Ground sequel to underline why Leeds moved to eclipse the previous record for Jordan Pickford.

    “England’s No 1” was a frequent chant from the travelling Leeds fans and although it may take some time for him to dislodge Pickford as the country’s first-choice, he is loving life at his new club.

    Trafford produced a number of fine saves and goals from Daniel James and James Justin secured a comfortable Carabao Cup second-round victory for Leeds, who also won here in the league on Saturday.

    Dan James has put Leeds ahead against Nottingham Forest 💥 pic.twitter.com/BdiYMXFJ5h.

    Leeds manager Daniel Farke said: “He has the potential to be one of the best goalkeepers in the Premier League and that is why Thomas Tuchel has picked him for England.

    “I like his natural confidence and aura, he knows that he’s good and he will be outstanding one day.

    “He has major chances to be under the spotlight and we are very pleased with him so far.”.

    Forest manager Oliver Glasner will be pleased to see the back of Leeds. He was appointed by Forest for the primary reason of winning trophies after successful tenures with Crystal Palace and Eintracht Frankfurt, but this particular avenue is now closed for this season.

    Four-time League Cup winners, Forest endured a difficult evening following the pre-match news that they have agreed a £45m deal with Chelsea for striker Liam Delap.

    Forest have established a reputation for noisy transfer windows but are determined to focus on quality over quantity this year. With Delap to undergo a medical on Wednesday, Forest will then focus on signing a new right wing-back before the deadline.

    Newcastle’s Jacob Murphy has been discussed, though a move is now regarded as unlikely. There are understood to be other targets under consideration.

    According to recent reports, glasner has insisted he does not want Forest to panic, and it remains to be seen whether they do spring into life on the final day. He noted: “I am not a magician or the messiah and we cannot ignore the reality that Leeds are ahead of us at the moment.

    In a recent development, “For nine months last season we were fighting relegation, so the players know it is going to take a lot of work. I know exactly what we have to change and that is what we will do.

    “We are responsible and made so many mistakes. Maybe we needed this result. At the moment we are far away from what we want but we will get there.”.

    This was a more open game than the attritional encounter from last weekend, as Trafford was forced into a fine early save to prevent Ola Aina’s cross from arcing into the top corner.

    Yet both teams were frequently making mistakes and providing masterclasses in how to misplace passes, frustrating their respective managers in the technical area.

    Industry observers note that the most impressive moment of the first-half came from Leeds centre-back Joe Rodon, racing back into position to deny Chris Wood from close range. Rodon celebrated the tackle as if it were a 30-yard screamer.

    It was always likely to be a mistake which proved the pivotal moment, and Arnaud Kalimuendo’s poor header cost the home team in the 50th minute.

    Kalimuendo’s error presented Sean Longstaff with space to run into and his pass found James, who beat Matz Sels with a clinical finish.

    “Can we play you every week?” was the inevitable chant from the travelling Leeds supporters.

    Forest’s fans were becoming twitchy and Trafford produced another save to frustrate Wood from eight yards after a break down the right from Kalimuendo.

    Glasner responded by making a quadruple substitution on the hour, yet Leeds remained dangerous and added a second goal 15 minutes from time when Justin bundled home after a goalmouth scramble.

    Ethan Ampadu's long throw causes CHAOS in the Forest box as Leeds go 2-0 up! pic.twitter.com/CtGDDIaRNp.

    You can catch the draw for the next stage of the League Cup on Sky Sports Main Event tomorrow night after the conclusion of Preston North End vs Everton.

    Nottingham Forest have agreed a club-record deal worth £45m for Chelsea forward Liam Delap.

    Delap has been deemed surplus to requirements at Stamford Bridge, and while the clubs were in talks over an initial loan deal, they have now struck a permanent agreement for the striker.

    The 23-year-old​ only signed for Chelsea in a £30m deal from Ipswich Town 12 months ago​ ​and is scheduled for a medical on Wednesday​. He will become Forest’s most expensive signing with the deal eclipsing the £37.5m they paid for Omari Hutchinson last summer.

    Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a new forward and Delap was a long-term target for the Austrian since his time as Crystal Palace head coach.

    Delap held talks with Forest last year over a potential move, and was also understood to have spoken with Glasner while he was at Palace.

    It has been revealed that speaking to ITV after the win, Rodon said: “I thought we were a bit sharper going forward, maybe a bit naive in the first half. I thought we had a lot of good chances maybe could have scored a couple of goals but we know it’s a difficult place to come and overall very happy to keep a clean sheet and win the game.”.

    Of his last-ditch tackle in the first half, he added: “We love it, as defenders it’s as good as a goal. I’m delighted, [keeping] clean sheets is my job and overall I got it right in the end.”.

    "There's a healthy arrogance about Leeds""Farke has gone from strength to strength"Izzy Christiansen and Jobi McAnuff praise the impact of Daniel Farke at Leeds 📈 pic.twitter.com/fgzLWRk3U2.

    "It's a bit soon to say Wembley!" 😅James Justin and Dan James react to Leeds progressing into round three of the Carabao Cup 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/m81C6eJT7C.

    Aug 30: Leeds United vs BrentfordSep 5: Brighton and Hove Albion vs Leeds UnitedSep 14: Leeds United vs Newcastle UnitedSep 19: Leeds United vs Crystal PalaceOct 10: Arsenal vs Leeds United.

    Aug 29: Liverpool vs Nottingham ForestSep 5: Nottingham Forest vs Tottenham HotspurSep 12: Aston Villa vs Nottingham ForestSep 19: Nottingham Forest vs CoventryOct 11: Crystal Palace vs Nottingham Forest.

    A tough night for the home teams...

    Cardiff City 1 Norwich 2Doncaster Rovers 1 Middlesbrough 3Barnsley 3 Crewe Alexandra 2Blackburn Rovers 1 Sheffield United 2Blackpool 1 Lincoln City 4Cambridge United 0 Millwall 1Fleetwood Town 4 Shrewsbury Town 0Ipswich Town 3 Leicester City 1Plymouth 2 Coventry City 4Sheffield Wednesday 0 Wolverhampton Wanderers 2Southampton 1 West Ham United 4Stevenage Town 0 Reading 3Stoke City 1 Hull City 1 (4-5 pens)Walsall 0 Leyton Orient 0 (5-6 pens)Watford 1 Peterborough United 5Birmingham City 1 Brentford 6Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 2.

    Industry observers note that and that is it. Two home defeats by Leeds in less than 80 hours for Forest. Glasner will have much to ponder with a daunting trip to Anfield coming up on Saturday. All smiles for Farke’s side.

    A look at a third for Leeds. Aaronson drives forward before setting Wilson who in turn lays on a first-time pass to Calvert-Lewin. The forward attempts to take his shot first time but can’t get the requisite power on the ball to beat Sels.

    A pitch invader makes a brief appearance on the turf but is swiftly ushered away.

    There is a late chance for Forest. Hutchinson’s cross is helped on by Dominguez but that touch inadvertently takes the ball away from Ndoye at the back post.

    Forest fans are filing out of the exits and who can blame them?

    There will be six minutes of added time.

    Recent findings suggest that that just about sums up Forest’s night. Dominguez stands over a free-kick from a dangerous area and, with the box loaded with their most imposing aerial threats, the midfielder sends the ball well over their heads and out for a goal-kick. So poor.

    Industry observers note that calvert-Lewin is now on for Nmecha. Not really the striker Forest defenders would want to see at this stage of the game.

    Another set-piece, this time a Stach corner, is barely dealt with by Forest.

    There’s a shout for a handball at the other end as Ndoye spears a cross into the body of Elvedi, but the referee rightly waves the appeals away.

    In a recent development, the “oles” ring out from the away end as Leeds string a series of passes together in the corner right in front of it. Forest are looking rather helpless here.

    Industry observers note that nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 2 (Justin) Ampadu introduces a throw-in from the right but has to reload as the referee notices some pushing in the box. His next attempt is far too loopy but causes Forest all sorts of trouble, bouncing and bobbling, and coming all the way through a thicket of limbs to Nmecha at the far post. Williams attempts to keep the ball out from a prone position on the goalline under pressure from Justin, who gets the final touch as the ball is bundled over the line.

    It's messy but Leeds won't care! 😁Forest fail to deal with the throw-in and Nmecha is there to bundle it in...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/oV46fs5RmP.

    In a recent development, jair goes into the book after catching Ampadu in full flight. He never had a prayer of reaching that ball.

    The resulting free-kick lands to Amapadu himself in the box, but his effort is deflected behind for a corner which is not up to much.

    Goalscorer James is taken off for Bogle, who will offer more mettle down Leeds’ right side as Forest search for an equaliser in the closing stages.

    In a recent development, stach has only been on the field for a matter of seconds but comes within a few inches of scoring. Wilson does well on the edge of the box before laying the ball to Stach whose curled effort grazes the outside of the side-netting.

    Longstaff’s final contribution to this game is a foul and yellow card as he spreads his legs wide to stop Ndoye breaking away through the middle.

    He is replaced by Wilson, as Tanaka and Okafaor also make way, for Stach and Aaronson.

    There’s plenty more endeavour down Forest’s new-look left side. Hudson Odoi scampers down that flank before cutting inside, and while he’s unable to fashion a chance the intent is correct.

    The substitutions appear to have breathed life into this Forest side. Murillo picks out Dominguez charging forward and Trafford does well to tip the midfielder’s effort behind. The resulting corner comes to nothing.

    Industry observers note that glasner resolves he has seen enough and rings the changes. Diomande, Aina, Jesus and Kalimuendo are replaced by Murillo, Netz, Ndoye and Hudson Odoi.

    Okafor demonstrates off his dancing feet in the Forest box, pulling off a few stepovers before the ball comes to Ampadu on the edge of the area but his strike is dragged wide.

    Chances at both ends! Kalimuendo plays a wonderful ball into the box for Wood to sweep home but Trafford springs into action and makes a stunning save.

    Leeds go up the other end, Okafor profiting from a diversionary run from centre-back Elvedi but cannot find the target and double Forest’s lead.

    End-to-end football! ⚡️First Wood, then Okafor - just 19 seconds between the two chances 😮#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/TGQmtwLNwE.

    Leeds are ahead and the inevitable chant from the away supporters is “can we play you every week?”.

    This is of course their second meeting in four days and Leeds are on course to record the double.

    Forest’s fans are starting to get a little twitchy.

    Sources indicate that dan James puts Leeds United in front! ⚽️Tidy finish from the Welshman... #EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/GzWg6zLGLm.

    Industry observers note that nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 1 (James) We finally have a breakthrough. Kalimuendo gives the ball up cheaply in the middle of the park and Longstaff is there to pick up the pieces, darting infield before laying on a perfectly weighted for James to gallop on to, take a touch and sweep beyond Sels. The winger has been Leeds’ biggest threat and deserves that goal.

    James finds space down the right - again - and his cross is closed down and deflected behind for a corner.

    Longstaff’s floated delivery is tipped away by Sels, but it turns out that the ball went out before coming in so a Forest goal kick is awarded.

    A lovely rendition of Mull of Kintyre precedes a short blast of the referee’s whistle and we’re back under way...

    Schlager goes into the book instantly for grabbing a handful of Tanaka’s shirt as the Japan international attempted to escape his clutches.

    This hasn’t been much of an improvement from Saturday.

    Both teams are producing masterclasses in how to misplace passes. Oliver Glasner and Daniel Farke have spent much of the first half looking very frustrated.

    James Trafford must be feeling very comfortable and confident of a second successive clean sheet after joining from Manchester City.

    Let’s hope for an improvement in the second-half.

    Should the scores remain level after 90 minutes, we will go straight to penalties. There’s still a half to play of course, but Forest’s League Cup shoot-out record should be a source of confidence having won seven from eight.

    Leeds have only won four from 10.

    What a tackle from Joe Rodon! 💥#EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/p5GkzSFEoZ.

    According to recent reports, james wins the ball on the halfway line and feeds Okafor down the left. He attempts a deft through-ball into a thicket of bodies but it comes to nothing.

    Leeds circulate the ball, working the ball from side to side but there is nowhere near enough movement in front of the ball-player for any meaningful forward passes to be played.

    And, quite aptly, the referee blows up at three seconds past 45 minutes. Certainly not a half for the books.

    Another half-chance for Forest! Milenkovic lands on a second ball off a deep free-kick but he cannot keep his strike down. A classic centre-half’s effort if you will.

    It has been revealed that ampadu comes over to the left to fire in a long throw-in. Sels comes steaming out of his goal and fumbles the ball but is awarded a free-kick after Muharemovic makes contact. Looked very minimal in all fairness.

    Industry observers note that oof, a good chance for Aina! Williams’ cross from the left comes all the way through to his opposite wing-back, but Aina’s half-volley sails over. A cracking contact, though.

    Sources indicate that elvedi and Muharemovic look to be astute buys from Leeds’ perspective. Both assured at the back and the latter especially is confident progressing the ball.

    Just as I type that Forest threaten with a ball over the top, but Justin nips in to take the ball away from Wood.

    Another decent opening for Leeds after a Forest turnover. Nmecha strides through the middle but Milenkovic is in position to ensure his run comes to nothing.

    What a tackle! Kalimuendo bursts through the middle after Leeds cede possession in a dangerous position. The winger plays in Wood who looks to be through on goal but Rodon comes out of nowhere to telescope a limb and stop the forward in his tracks. Fantastic defensive work from the Welshman.

    Nmecha attempts to break beyond the halfway line but is stymied by a swarm of Forest players. He demands a foul from the referee who is not interested in the least.

    It’s then Okafor’s turn to put in a dangerous cross from the left, but Nmecha cannot get to it.

    Tanaka becomes the first man to go into the book. The ball gets away from him and Jesus puts body between man and ball smartly to win the foul.

    Tanaka is now dropping into the back line to allow Leeds’ defenders the licence to get wider and higher. Forest will need to be wary of their opponents’ numerical advantage down the flanks.

    The game has reached something of a holding pattern as both sides resolve to slow things down, at least temporarily. Forest have settled into a slightly deeper block.

    Sensing an opportunity, Ampadu spins in a glorious through-ball between centre-back and full-back for James to gallop on to. He hits the by-line and cuts back to Longstaff, but the midfielder can’t beat Sels. A good chance that probably should have been converted.

    Sources indicate that A good chance goes begging! 🫣Longstaff is free for Leeds but fires it straight at Sels...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/0UJdfSDQ6w.

    Tanaka then turns provider, winning possession in Forest’s half before playing in Longstaff, whose cross-cum-shot does not threaten Sels’ goal.

    Recent findings suggest that both sides have physical, quick out-balls, which has made for a frenetic encounter thus far. James rasps in another fierce cross from the right after another sweeping Leeds move, but Nmecha cannot get there and Tanaka fires well over on the follow-up.

    Aina’s throw-in, this time from the left, is flicked on to Jesus at the back post and while the forward is able to direct the ball goalwards there is Justin on the line to clear the ball to safety.

    It has been revealed that chance! Dominguez slides in Aina down the right channel and the full-back’s mishit cross has Trafford scrambling. He palms the ball behind for a corner, which is headed away for a Forest throw-in on the far side.

    Leeds are enjoying a spell of possession here, Tanaka and Longstaff peeling off into the wide areas to collect the ball and disrupt Forest’s mid-block out-of-possession structure. The hosts are more than happy for Leeds to circulate the ball in front of their first line of pressure as, for the second time tonight, Trafford boots it out into touch.

    Recent findings suggest that dominguez stands up a smart cross to the far post where Aina is waiting to head back across goal. Trafford backpedals into Kalimuendo and the referee awards Leeds a free-kick.

    Wonderful touch there early in the game from none other than Oliver Glasner.

    Forest’s head coach perfectly trapped a high ball as it landed towards him in the technical area.

    James indicates off his speed for the first time tonight, accelerating down the right before fizzing a dangerous ball into the six-yard box but Forest clear their lines.

    Sels goes long to Wood (feels like the right play given his attributes), James lands on the second ball but can only boot the ball into row Z to jeers from the home fans.

    Aina rolls out a long throw-in from the right and it’s headed behind for a corner. Trafford punches the inswinging delivery away and Williams’ effort from the edge of the box sails well over.

    Forest are in their red home shirts, kicking from left to right. Leeds are in their yellow away number. Same set-up as the weekend.

    It has been revealed that players and mascots walk on to the City Ground turf. A place in the League Cup third round on the line.

    Sources indicate that the first pre-match question put to Glasner by ITV was in relation to the reported £45m club-record deal for Chelsea forward Liam Delap. He responded: “I can tell everybody that he doesn’t play today. Everything else we shall see in the next days.”.

    Oliver Glasner breaks his silence on Nottingham Forest's record signing, Liam Delap 🚨He speaks to @gabrielclarke05 ahead of Forest's Carabao Cup tie against Leeds 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/8DlWMIzVS9.

    Recent findings suggest that reflecting on Saturday’s defeat by Leeds in his programme notes, Glasner wrote: “I saw plenty of encouraging signs from the team on Saturday and I felt we were a lot closer to scoring than we were conceding, especially in the second half. Unfortunately, the small margins were not on our side.

    “I thought our defence looked comfortable, but there is still work to be done and the more the players get used to the system we’re operating, the more we’ll see that work come to fruition in competitive matches.

    “We have recovered well and will be ready to give our all this evening.”.

    Previewing tonight’s League Cup match, Leeds head coach Daniel Farke remarked: “Our league win is good for our mood and confidence, but this is a ‘do or die’ cup game. Both teams will be motivated to progress, so I expect a tight game. It will be difficult to win on the road again against a tough opponent.”.

    When asked what winning a first trophy of his managerial career would mean to him, Farke added: “Well, we weren’t too far away last season. Overall, I would say my form in cup competitions hasn’t been too bad during my career. I’m a big believer in these competitions, I like the ‘do or die’ mentality. I would never say no to another good cup run.”.

    The hosts’ kits tonight will include Carabao Cup sleeve patches with the number four on them, in recognition of the club’s League Cup triumphs in 1978, 1979, 1989 and 1990.

    🏆x4⃣ pic.twitter.com/DRPXFa2kM3.

    This is Forest and Leeds Part 2, just four days after they clashed in the Premier League.

    Daniel Farke ruined the Oliver Glasner welcoming party on Saturday with a 1-0 smash-and-grab victory at the death.

    Both managers have gone relatively strong for this tie, with only a sprinkling of debuts.

    Ousmane Diomande, the £34m signing from Sporting, makes his first appearance while there is a first start for Xaver Schlager.

    Leeds have given a debut to Switzerland defender Nico Elvedi.

    Nottingham Forest Sels; Diomande, Jair, Milenkovic; Aina, Schlager, Dominguez, Williams; Jesus, Kalimuendo; Wood.

    Subs Victor, Murillo, Abbott, Netz, Hutchinson, Ndoye, McAtee, Sangare, Hudson Odoi.

    Leeds United Trafford; Rodon, Elvedi, Muharemovic; Ampadu, Tanaka, Longstaff, Justin; James, Okafor; Nmecha.

    Subs Perri, Lienou, Bijol, Bogle, Wilson, Cresswell, Stach, Aaronson, Calvert-Lewin.

    The massive breaking news is that Forest are smashing their club record to sign Chelsea forward Liam Delap for £45m.

    Delap will undergo a medical at Forest on Wednesday with the deal potentially rising to £50m after add-ons.

    It eclipses the previous transfer record of £37.5m for winger Omari Hutchinson.

    Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a fresh centre-forward this summer and Delap ticks pretty much every box for him.

    Farke makes six changes to the complement that started against Forest in the league on Saturday.

    Recent findings suggest that 📋 Your #LUFC XI... pic.twitter.com/XuUzwwkmfi.

    Wood makes Glasner’s XI while summer acquisitions Diomande and Schlager are handed their first competitive Forest starts.

    Recent findings suggest that our @Carabao_Cup XI this evening. 📋 pic.twitter.com/Wv918WJScj.

    It has been revealed that welcome to live coverage of the Carabao Cup second-round match between Nottingham Forest and Leeds United. This will be the sides’ second meeting at the City Ground in four days after Anton Stach’s late free-kick decided an attritional contest on the Premier League’s opening weekend. Forest’s new head coach Oliver Glasner is something of a cup specialist, though, with FA Cup, Europa League and Conference League titles to his name and he will relish the opportunity to right the wrongs of Saturday in front of the Forest faithful.

    The Austrian is Forest’s fifth head coach in less than 12 months and he will look to arrest the churn by bringing to the City Ground the success he enjoyed with Crystal Palace. During pre-season, the Austrian moulded Forest into his preferred 3-4-3 shape, placing summer acquisition Ousmane Diomande alongside the existing central-defensive partnership of Murillo and Nikola Milenković. Here, Diomande gets his Forest debut and Glasner brings in talisman Chris Wood from the start.

    Daniel Farke will have been delighted to see his Leeds side continue their excellent form in pre-season – which included victories over Liverpool, Red Bull Leipzig and Augsburg – into the season proper. Although Leeds arrive at the City Ground shorn of attacking options Wilfried Gnonto, Noah Okafor and Mateo Joseph through injury, Farke still shuffles the pack in the forward positions with this weekend’s visit of Brentford to Elland Road in mind.

    Ward getting ruthless: Liverpool ‘have already decided’ to let Kop favourite leave for free

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (549 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Empireofthekop

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Liverpool are ready to let a long-serving stalwart leave Anfield for free in 2027, according to one insider.
    • The last player standing from the tail end of Brendan Rodgers’ managerial reign, Joe Gomez is now into his 12th season with the Reds, albeit that he’s been consigned to a backup role thus far under Andoni Iraola.
    • The 29-year-old has featured for just 259 minutes across our 16 matches so far in this campaign, more than half of which have come in the Carabao Cup (Transfermarkt), and as it stand he’ll be out of contract in seven months’ time.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Liverpool are ready to let a long-serving stalwart leave Anfield for free in 2027, according to one insider.

    The last player standing from the tail end of Brendan Rodgers’ managerial reign, Joe Gomez is now into his 12th season with the Reds, albeit that he’s been consigned to a backup role thus far under Andoni Iraola.

    The 29-year-old has featured for just 259 minutes across our 16 matches so far in this campaign, more than half of which have come in the Carabao Cup (Transfermarkt), and as it stand he’ll be out of contract in seven months’ time.

    Ex-Manchester United chief scout Mick Brown has claimed that Liverpool sporting director Julian Ward has already decided that the club’s longest-serving current player won’t be offered a new deal, with injury challenges not helping the defender’s case.

    Industry observers note that he told Football Insider: “Liverpool have already decided they’re going to let Joe Gomez leave. He doesn’t have much of a role to play at the moment, he’s not starting games at right-back even despite their injuries, and he isn’t competing for a centre-back position.

    Sources indicate that “His injuries are always a concern as well. They don’t think he can start games consistently, and all of these challenges stack up eventually.

    “It would be a surprise to me if they were to offer him a newly introduced contract, especially when you consider they’re going to be looking to bring in new defenders at some stage.

    “If he hasn’t played much this season, that’s not going to change with fresh players coming in, so I expect he’ll be allowed to look at what other options might be available.”.

    Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

    Ward could be quite busy with contract renewals over the next few months, with Alisson Becker, Virgil van Dijk and Alexis Mac Allister reportedly all in line for prospective new deals.

    Whereas that trio are virtually guaranteed to start, though, Gomez usually has to rely on substitute appearances or heavy squad rotation for domestic cup games, and it’s not implausible that he could be allowed to depart on a free transfer next summer.

    If that is indeed his fate, he’ll be assured of a raucous send-off at Anfield on the final day of the season, with his popularity among the fan base unmistakably evident by the roar which greeted his successful penalty in the Carabao Cup shootout triumph over Chelsea last month.

    As Lewis Steele rightly mentioned, the 29-year-old ‘very rarely puts a foot wrong’ whenever he’s called upon, and even if he isn’t getting much game-time, we don’t doubt that he’s imparting some invaluable advice to the young defenders at Liverpool who can learn so much from him.

    If this is to be Gomez’s last campaign with the Reds, all we ask is that he does finally, finally get his first goal for the club during regulation time. You’d be very hard pressed to find a more popular goalscorer if that moment were to happen!

    #50532. Savio scores on debut as Spurs cruise past Charlton in Carabao Cup
