    Savio scores on debut as Spurs cruise past Charlton in Carabao Cup

    📅 26 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 19 min read (3805 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~19 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It looked like this was going to be a night for “one of their own”, but Tottenham Hotspur’s latest big-money arrival, Sávio, stole the headlines to crank up the excitement at his newly introduced club.
    • Mikey Moore had set Spurs on their way to what proved a comfortable Carabao Cup success over Championship club Charlton Athletic and heard his name sung by the home fans.
    • But Sávio stepped off the substitutes’ bench to take the limelight with a late goal just a few days after completing his expensive switch from Manchester City, and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is demanding many more to come.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It looked like this was going to be a night for “one of their own”, but Tottenham Hotspur’s latest big-money arrival, Sávio, stole the headlines to crank up the excitement at his newly introduced club.

    Mikey Moore had set Spurs on their way to what proved a comfortable Carabao Cup success over Championship club Charlton Athletic and heard his name sung by the home fans.

    But Sávio stepped off the substitutes’ bench to take the limelight with a late goal just a few days after completing his expensive switch from Manchester City, and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is demanding many more to come.

    Recent findings suggest that “A perfect day for him,” said De Zerbi. “His biggest improvement is to increase the number of goals. He is one of the best wingers, but the best wingers score many goals and I spoke with him two days ago, and we put the goal at 10-12 goals.

    “We need 10-12 goals from the wingers. Last season, we suffered too much because the number of goals were not enough.”.

    According to recent reports, "What an introduction!"Sávio scores a brilliant goal on his Spurs debut! 👏 pic.twitter.com/WgmcfgeNpX.

    Having watched some of Tottenham’s signings fall to a 3-0 Premier League defeat by Brentford a few days earlier, Sávio’s late impact was the perfect lift for the Spurs supporters.

    The club have committed to spending almost £400m this summer, leading to debate by outsiders over whether it will prove to be money well spent and huge waves of excitement within the fanbase.

    A deal that could be worth as much as £85m, if add-ons are achieved, for Sávio certainly raised some eyebrows, but the Brazilian provided the perfect response by scoring just 11 minutes into his debut as a late substitute.

    It has been revealed that in the 82nd minute, Sávio cut in from the flank and scored with a shot past Charlton goalkeeper Tiernan Brooks. He and the Spurs crowd thought he had a second a few minutes later, but his shot hit Ben Davies on its way into the net and the defender was credited with the goal.

    Having sung for Moore earlier in the game, the Spurs fans wasted no time in trying out their new song for Sávio, inspired by the Spandau Ballet hit Gold.

    Moore has been expected to move to Cologne on loan, but provided a reminder of his talent by opening the scoring in the first half with only his second goal for the club.

    What a hit from Mikey Moore! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/OgSM4qhiqs.

    “We have to understand the best solution,” De Zerbi remarked. “I would like to keep him. He’s young but a good player, but we can’t make the wrong decision. He needs to play, he needs to get games inside him.”.

    Sources indicate that cutting in from the right, where Sávio is primed to play, Moore surged past his marker and shot from just inside the box. Brooks should have stopped it, but the ball flew past him and into the net.

    Three minutes after Moore’s opener, Dominic Solanke scored his first goal since March to offer a reminder of what he can still give De Zerbi, who is poised to welcome Omar Marmoush to Tottenham.

    Buoyed by his first-half goal, Moore skipped his way around a couple of tackles at the start of the second period but his low cross was cut out. The Spurs fans responded by singing “he’s one of our own.”.

    Substitute Kevin Danso netted with his first touch from a header, before Sávio was introduced to steal the show, despite a late consolation goal from Charlton’s Lloyd Jones.

    Kevin Danso scores with his first touch since coming on! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/oqUU7wjoJW.

    The victory set up a tough third-round trip to Anfield to face Liverpool for Tottenham, but De Zerbi noted: “It’s a great game. If we want to win the competition we have to win the games.

    Sources indicate that “Sometimes in this competition, it can happen that you play against big teams. It’s a great challenge for the players, for me, for our clubs. We have to arrive ready to play in our style, with personality, ready to play a game following the work we are doing on the training ground.”.

    Leyton Orient vs BradfordReading vs BrentfordPeterborough vs BarnsleyWest Ham vs Fulham or AFC Wimbledon.

    Chelsea or Luton vs LeedsMillwall vs NewcastleFleetwood vs Sheffield UnitedEverton vs Wolves.

    Ipswich vs ArsenalCoventry vs Aston VillaBournemouth vs LincolnLiverpool vs Tottenham.

    The ties are starting to come through, with 16 to come in total. Here are the first few to trickle through:.

    Crystal Palace vs MiddlesbroughManchester United vs BrightonManchester City vs NorwichSunderland vs Hull City.

    In a recent development, “He did great when he came on. He is going to be a joy for all of us to watch. I am sure he will be a fan favourite. He revealed what a player he is tonight. To get one goal and an assist on his debut is great.”.

    Premier League: Brighton, Arsenal, Brentford, Everton, Hull, Ipswich, Manchester City, Liverpool, Newcastle, Bournemouth, Sunderland, Crystal Palace, Manchester United, Coventry, Tottenham, Aston Villa.

    Championship: Millwall, Wolves, Middlesbrough, Sheffield United, West Ham, Lincoln, Norwich.

    League One: Bradford, Leyton Orient, Peterborough, Reading, Barnsley.

    Still to play: Chelsea v Luton, Fulham v AFC Wimbledon.

    The teams in the hat for the League Cup third round will found out who they will face very shortly and we will let you know all the ties for the third round.

    Bradford 0 Burnley 0 (Bradford won 4-2 on penalties)Newcastle 3 West Brom 2Tottenham 5 Charlton 1Preston 0 Everton 4.

    Possession: Tottenham 73%-27% CharltonShots: 20-6Shots on target: 11-4Corners: 11-6Touches in opposition box: 45-8.

    It is all over in north London and Tottenham have booked their place in the third round of the League Cup with a comfortable 5-1 win over Charlton.

    Three added minutes in north London.

    Newcastle have just about got past West Brom, winning 3-2 in the end, and they book their place in the third round.

    Sources indicate that at least the travelling Charlton fans have something to cheer about even if their side are being dumped out of the League Cup. A corner from the left comes to the back post, where Jones rises highest to head it between Kinsky’s legs and into the Tottenham net.

    Sources indicate that savio thinks he has his second in quick succession but it will go down as Davies’ goal. Savio’s shot was on target but it deflects off Davies and goes in for Tottenham’s fifth on the night.

    The Brazilian signed just yesterday but he now has a first Tottenham goal to his name. He cuts inside from the right and drives across the face of the penalty area before firing at the near post, beating Brooks. Tottenham are cruising into the third round and their newest signing scores on his debut.

    According to recent reports, "What an introduction!"Sávio scores a brilliant goal on his Spurs debut! 👏 pic.twitter.com/WgmcfgeNpX.

    Tottenham are cruising into the third round and so are Everton, who lead Preston by the same scoreline. Newcastle lead West Brom 3-2 whilst it is still 0-0 between Bradford and Burnley.

    Change for Tottenham as Williams-Barnett replaces Tel.

    Tel crosses from the left side of the box and picks out Savio, who attempts an audacious flick that does not come off.

    West Brom were not back on level terms for long as Barnes has his second of the game and Newcastle lead 3-2 with under 10 minutes remaining.

    Charlton have barely threatened the Tottenham goal tonight but that is a decent opportunity for Leaburn, who is played in down the right and forces Kinsky into a decent save.

    Savio is straight into the action with good work down the right and squares it for Tel, whose shot is straight at Brooks.

    Savio is on for his Tottenham debut and replaces Solanke. Savio only joined Tottenham yesterday but makes his first appearance for the club tonight.

    In a recent development, newcastle had fought from 1-0 down against West Brom to lead 2-1 but Hall has just given away a penalty for the second time in a matter of days having also conceded one in the dying moments of their 2-2 draw against Liverpool on Sunday. Price has stepped up to score his second of the game to bring West Brom level at 2-2 with just over 10 minutes to go.

    Industry observers note that the Austrian defender has just come on and, with his first touch, puts Tottenham 3-0 up. Fernandes’ free-kick from just outside the box on the right is met by Danso, who attacks it and his header finds the bottom corner. You have to say that goal was coming. Danso has hurt himself as there was a clash of heads as he met the delivery and receives treatment to his head.

    Kevin Danso scores with his first touch since coming on! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/oqUU7wjoJW.

    Roberto De Zerbi is turning to his bench and making a triple change as Van de Ven, Danso and Porro come on.

    Charlton are also making a triple change of their own.

    Gray is found on the left side of the Charlton penalty area and he drives his shot towards goal, forcing Brooks into a decent save. Tottenham are pushing for that third goal.

    A cross is sent in from the right and it comes to Tel, who volleys first time but it is a fairly routine save for Brooks in the Charlton goal.

    Tottenham are starting to ramp up the pressure as they go in search of a third goal. As it stands, the only side that looks like scoring is Tottenham.

    Plenty of cheers from the home fans as Savio is out to warm up. Will Roberto De Zerbi turn to the Brazilian and give him his debut tonight?

    One of the fresh laws brought in this season is to speed up throw-ins and Gray falls foul of taking too long, with Charlton then being given the throw-in.

    Tel decides to shoot from range after Charlton clear a corner but the Frenchman’s effort is straight at Brooks.

    Play has resumed in north London, with Tottenham 2-0 up over Charlton.

    They are back under way at St James’ Park and there has been a goal within a few minutes of the second half starting. Newcastle were 1-0 down against West Brom but they now lead 2-1 thanks to Barnes’ goal.

    Possession: Tottenham 76%-24% CharltonShots: 9-2Shots on target: 4-1Corners: 7-2Touches in opposition box: 25-2.

    The first half in north London is brought to an end and Tottenham take a 2-0 lead into the break thanks to goals from Moore and Solanke. Tottenham looked rather lethargic for a lot of that first half but two goals in quick succession has Roberto De Zerbi’s side in control. As the players head off, the DJ pays homage to the late Dolly Parton by blasting out Nine to Five.

    Whilst they are still in added time in north London, it is half-time at St James’ Park and Newcastle are level 1-1 with West Brom.

    Apter is booked for cynically tripping up Udogie.

    Due to a few Charlton injuries, there will be six added minutes.

    Like London buses, two goals come in quick succession and Tottenham have their second just before the break. Charlton fail to clear their lines inside their own box before Solanke volleys in on the swivel from the penalty spot. Charlton will feel that was definitely an avoidable goal.

    Tottenham had looked rather lethargic but they take the lead in emphatic style. The 19-year-old cuts inside from the right and comes across the face of the Charlton penalty area. Moore then strikes it powerfully with his left foot and the ball flies into the roof of the net. Could Brooks have done better in the Charlton goal? Moore will not care.

    Sources indicate that what a hit from Mikey Moore! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/OgSM4qhiqs.

    Tottenham are right now too slow in possession and are not moving the ball promptly enough, meaning it is easier for Charlton to defend.

    West Brom had taken the lead at St James’ Park but Newcastle are back on level terms through summer signing Toure.

    According to recent reports, A corner from the right ends up coming out to the edge of the box, where Tel takes it first time but his volley goes a long way wide. That moment sums up Tottenham’s evening thus far.

    Sources indicate that solanke has a shot from the edge of the box blocked before Gray’s effort with the outside of his right foot is saved well by Brooks down to his left. That looked like it was creeping in so Brooks had to get a hand to that.

    Industry observers note that charlton play the corner short and eventually the ball comes in. Asiimwe meets it and has a good chance from eight yards out but his header goes just wide. That was a decent chance for Charlton.

    The first booking of the night goes the way of the hosts as Bergvall cynically takes down Apter as the Charlton man drove towards the Tottenham penalty area. You feel like Charlton need to take advantage of opportunities like this if they want to win this tie. The ball is clipped in and it comes off Van Hecke’s head for a corner. Tottenham clear their lines initially but Charlton keep it alive. Docherty strikes it first time from the edge of the Tottenham box and forces Kinsky into a good save diving to his left.

    Sources indicate that that probably sums up Tottenham’s night thus far. Davies pings a lovely diagonal ball out to Moore in space down Tottenham’s right. Moore waits for the overlapping run of Gray before playing the pass but Gray’s attempted cross from the right side of the box is terrible and goes behind for a goal kick. Roberto De Zerbi is quickly out of his seat!

    In a recent development, roberto De Zerbi was keen to see his side show a reaction to their defeat at Brentford on Saturday. Unsurprisingly, they are dominating possession but have not posed much of a threat going forward.

    In a recent development, there has been a goal at St James’ Park and it is the visitors West Brom who have taken the lead over Newcastle. Price has scored directly from a free-kick and the Championship side lead.

    A sensational free-kick from Isaac Price to give West Brom the lead at St. James' Park! 🤯Watch the Carabao Cup here! - https://t.co/4BMyhp9stB pic.twitter.com/Pnt78LWFN6.

    It has been revealed that things have just gone from bad to worse for Charlton. Whilst one of their centre-backs is being stretchered off in Sichenje, their other centre-half Koumetio, who used to be on the books at Liverpool, is also down. Koumetio, like Sichenje, is going to come off. McNamara and Jones, who like Koumetio used to be at Liverpool, are coming on. Charlton have had to change both centre-backs inside the opening quarter of an hour.

    In a recent development, sichenje did try to continue but he has gone back down again and his night appears to be over. The question will be has he done more damage to his knee trying to play on? The stretcher is being brought on and it will be a sorry end to his night.

    Moore wins Tottenham a corner out on the right, which summer signing Fernandes will take. His delivery is headed away and the danger is gone.

    Sichenje has now got back to his feet so he may have avoided a serious injury but we will see if he can continue. It looks like he will try to continue at least.

    Recent findings suggest that play is halted as Charlton defender Sichenje looks to be in a lot of pain as he bangs the ground in frustration. It appears to be his left knee and the visitors may be forced into an early change.

    Inside the opening minute, Solanke thinks he will have a chance on goal as the ball is played in behind but there is too much on it and the ball goes through to Brooks in the Charlton goal.

    We are under way in north London.

    Both sides emerge from the tunnel at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and we are just moments away from kick-off north London. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:.

    Tottenham: Kinsky; Gray, Van Hecke, Davies, Udogie; Fernandes, Bentancur, Bergvall; Moore, Solanke, Tel. Substitutes: Dubravka, Robertson, Danso, Gallagher, Richarlison, Savio, Porro, Van de Ven, Williams-Barnett.

    Charlton: Brooks, Shichenje, Koumetio, Mesik, Asilmwe, Knibbs, Ouma, Apter, Docherty, Alli, Mbick.Substitutes: Okonkwo, Jones, Coventry, Leaburn, Carey, McNamara, Rankin-Costello, Nwamba, Tagoe.

    It has been revealed that “Tottenham are a top club. Top manager and players so it is a wonderful opportunity to test ourselves. We need to be organised and in the moments we have we want to use our structure to carry a threat. We want to see our structure coming through because we want to evolve. We are a way off these yet, but that is eventually the goal.”.

    "They got what they deserved"Jamie Redknapp on Spurs' opening day loss against Brentford 😤 pic.twitter.com/mLEb1cCF1x.

    "I would like to see a reaction"Roberto De Zerbi speaks ahead of Spurs vs Charlton 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/dVIqQBG3wV.

    After nine years at Anfield, Andy Robertson has swapped Liverpool for Tottenham this summer. He started for Tottenham against Brentford and is on the bench tonight ahead of what could be his first home game for the club.

    Omar Marmoush will undergo a medical at Tottenham Hotspur on Wednesday on loan with an obligation to pay Manchester City £60m for the Egypt forward next summer.

    Marmoush will become the second signing from City this week after Savinho – who has asked to be referred to as Sávio – completed his move.

    City signed Marmoush two seasons ago from Eintracht Frankfurt for £59m and the German club do not have a sell-on clause, meaning they will not receive a fee from the deal.

    It has been revealed that tottenham: Kinsky; Gray, Van Hecke, Davies, Udogie; Fernandes, Bentancur, Bergvall; Moore, Solanke, Tel. Substitutes: Dubravka, Robertson, Danso, Gallagher, Richarlison, Savio, Porro, Van de Ven, Williams-Barnett.

    Charlton: Brooks, Shichenje, Koumetio, Mesik, Asilmwe, Knibbs, Ouma, Apter, Docherty, Alli, Mbick.Substitutes: Okonkwo, Jones, Coventry, Leaburn, Carey, McNamara, Rankin-Costello, Nwamba, Tagoe.

    We've arrived in N17 👋#cafc pic.twitter.com/5lq8FcrEfA.

    Sources indicate that we will also provide updates from Newcastle’s game against West Brom. The draw for League Cup third round will take place after all the games have been completed tonight.

    Savio only completed his move from Manchester City yesterday but he is on the bench for Tottenham tonight ahead of what looks set to be his debut for the north London club.

    Sávio in his upcoming home 😍 pic.twitter.com/tHBGFkq3DK.

    INS:Sandro Tonali ⇠ Newcastle, £100mMateus Fernandes ⇠ West Ham, £85mJan Paul van Hecke ⇠ Brighton, £55mMarcos Senesi ⇠ Bournemouth, FreeAndrew Robertson ⇠ Liverpool, FreeMartin Dubravka ⇠ Burnley, FreeSavio ⇠ Manchester City, £85m.

    You will likely be able to add Omar Marmoush’s name to the list of incomings very soon.

    TEAM NEWS! 🚨 Your Addicks to take on Spurs 🏆#cafc pic.twitter.com/uyH4dfH9CD.

    Sources indicate that our Spurs side to face Charlton! 📋🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/yQuEVgkHbm.

    According to recent reports, A place in the League Cup third round is at stake as Tottenham host Charlton in a London derby at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. The last competitive meeting between these sides came in the FA Cup back in January 2011, with Tottenham winning that game 3-0 at White Hart Lane. A then 19-year-old Andros Townsend made his debut that day and scored, with Jermain Defoe scoring a brace.

    Recent findings suggest that tottenham’s Premier League campaign got off to the worst possible start as they lost 3-0 at Brentford last weekend. Tottenham have been very busy during this summer transfer window and that has continued this week. Savio (formerly Savinho) has arrived from Manchester City in a deal that could be worth £85m and the Brazilian could make his Tottenham debut tonight, having been registered in time.

    Sources indicate that “I think in attacking positions we need players capable one-on one, to create something, to create a chance to score,” Roberto De Zerbi said. “In terms of one-on-one, he [Savio] is one of the best players, especially since 2024. He can play on the right side, on the left side. I have known him from a long time, I spoke with him when he went to Manchester City. He is a big player for us.

    “I do not know if I am the right man [to get the most out of Savio], but for sure he has to achieve. I think a player who is so good in one-on-one, so good at creating chances to score, to be complete, he has to score. If you analyse the other best wingers in the world, many of them, they score 10 to 15 goals per season. He has the qualities. Maybe his habits, he has to change habits, because he has to be focused on the assists, the one-on-one dribbling and also to score.”.

    Omar Marmoush is closing in on an initial loan deal from Manchester City but that move is not complete and thus he is not available for Tottenham tonight. Micky van der Ven and Pedro Porro are both available having missed Tottenham’s loss at Brentford but the hosts are still without Xavi Simons, Pape Sarr, Dejan Kulusevski and Wilson Odobert.

    Charlton have made the perfect start to their Championship campaign; a 2-1 home win over Derby was followed up by a 2-1 victory at recently-relegated West Ham. Nathan Jones’ side earned their place in the League Cup second round with a 3-1 win at Cheltenham in the first round.

    “We have to be very organised and very professional, they [Tottenham] are a top team,” Jones said. “They have a great manager and a brilliant group of players. They already had a Premier League squad and they have spent, what is reaching about, I do not know, £300 million or something like that. It is a wonderful test, we have to be right near our best and do both sides of the game very well. Of course, you want to test yourself against the best managers and you want to test yourself against the best teams. For us, this is not our priority, the Championship is our priority, but this is the next game and therefore it is the most key.”.

    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

    Champions League draw: Arsenal to renew Mourinho rivalry with Real Madrid tie

    📅 27 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2347 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Arsenal will host old nemesis José Mourinho’s Real Madrid in the league phase of the Champions League.
    • Mourinho, the former Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur manager, will return to London to resume hostilities against last season’s beaten finalists.
    • Other reunions from Thursday’s draw include Manchester City travelling to Barcelona, to whom they last week sold Rodri, and Liverpool visiting Inter Milan, who have signed Curtis Jones.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Arsenal will host old nemesis José Mourinho’s Real Madrid in the league phase of the Champions League.

    Mourinho, the former Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur manager, will return to London to resume hostilities against last season’s beaten finalists.

    Other reunions from Thursday’s draw include Manchester City travelling to Barcelona, to whom they last week sold Rodri, and Liverpool visiting Inter Milan, who have signed Curtis Jones.

    Arsenal will also travel to Harry Kane’s Bayern Munich, while United will host the Germans as well on their Champions League return in a repeat of the legendary 1999 final. Michael Carrick’s side will also visit Cesc Fàbregas’s Como.

    Mourinho last managed at the Emirates Stadium in March 2021, barely a month before his sacking by Spurs.

    During his two spells as Chelsea manager, Mourinho famously had run-ins with Arsenal’s Arsène Wenger.

    Mourinho called Wenger a “specialist in failure” after the Frenchman failed to add to his three Premier League titles following his Portuguese counterpart’s arrival in London in 2004.

    Last season, Mikel Arteta finally ended Arsenal’s long wait to be crowned champions of England but agonisingly missed out on European glory.

    Sources indicate that verdict Premier League champions should not be daunted by any game, but Real Madrid – with Mourinho in control – has the feel of a defining match of the group stage. Facing Kane in Munich does not seem any easier. Some tough assignments here including a trip to Napoli but the pot-four teams seem straightforward for Mikel Arteta.

    Industry observers note that verdict Playing against the European champions and travelling to Barcelona will be a true test of how much progress Enzo Maresca has made in the short time he has been at the Etihad Stadium. City’s other games do not look easy either but they should be defeating teams such as Sporting Lisbon and Porto – at least they would be expected to under Pep Guardiola.

    Verdict The San Siro was where Arne Slot began to turn results around last season and Iraola getting a win there would be a substantial statement.     • While the Los Angeles Rams try to make the most of a 2026 campaign that began with astronomical expectations, wide receiver Puka Nacua is already working toward 2027.
    • Based on that reported prognosis, the 25-year-old Nacua will miss the remainder of the regular season and the playoffs.
    • The two-time All-Pro wideout received recommendations from three doctors to undergo the procedure, per ESPN's latest report, which noted that team doctor Neal ElAttrache performed the operation.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    While the Los Angeles Rams try to make the most of a 2026 campaign that began with astronomical expectations, wide receiver Puka Nacua is already working toward 2027. He had MCL surgery on Tuesday, and his recovery timeline is considered to be four to five months, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported on Saturday night.

    Based on that reported prognosis, the 25-year-old Nacua will miss the remainder of the regular season and the playoffs.

    The two-time All-Pro wideout received recommendations from three doctors to undergo the procedure, per ESPN's latest report, which noted that team doctor Neal ElAttrache performed the operation.

    When the NFL confirmed this week that it was suspending Nacua three games for violating the league's personal conduct policy, it reportedly wasn't aware that he had already had surgery.

    The Rams placed Nacua on injured reserve with knee and turf toe injuries on Nov. 12, a week before the NFL imposed its suspension. Like any player who lands on IR, Nacua had to sit out four games before he could return. By the time the suspension was announced, the length of that ban and his remaining time on IR were aligned.

    While that situation understandably turned heads, it's worth noting that Nacua isn't the first player to serve a suspension while on IR.

    The last year has been a head-scratching one for Nacua, who's among the best wide receivers in the sport but has run into off-field trouble.

    This past offseason, news broke that a woman was suing Nacua. She alleged that, on Dec. 31, 2025, he made an antisemitic statement and later bit her on the shoulder. Nacua's attorney denied the woman's claim that he made such a comment and downplayed the biting as "horseplay.".

    Nacua voluntarily entered a holistic care facility in March to focus on his personal growth. He reflected on that experience in May.

    Industry observers note that in seven games this season, Nacua — the league's 2025 receptions leader — piled up 70 catches for 715 yards and 4 touchdowns. He also scored on the ground once for a 6-4 Rams team that's hardly had the start it envisioned this fall.

    According to recent reports, nacua's injuries occurred on the final offensive snap of L.A.'s Week 9 win over the Washington Commanders. He's in the last year of his rookie contract.

    Sources indicate that his future in L.A. has yet to be determined, and he won't be available for the Rams in the short term. That mentioned, the Rams are hoping to get veteran wide receiver Davante Adams back down the stretch, as they make a push for the playoffs.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Latest York Rangers goaltender Igor Shesterkin will miss the remainder of the season with a lower-body injury, the team unveiled on Saturday.
    • Sources indicate that shesterkin suffered an apparent leg injury in the Rangers' loss to the Washington Capitals on Friday night as his right leg slid awkwardly into the post while scrambling to get back in position.
    • Prior to that loss, the Rangers were off to a terrific 4-1-0 start, and Shesterkin was a driving force behind that success.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Latest York Rangers goaltender Igor Shesterkin will miss the remainder of the season with a lower-body injury, the team unveiled on Saturday.

    Sources indicate that shesterkin suffered an apparent leg injury in the Rangers' loss to the Washington Capitals on Friday night as his right leg slid awkwardly into the post while scrambling to get back in position. Shesterkin fell to the ice immediately, and he needed assistance to get down the tunnel.

    Prior to that loss, the Rangers were off to a terrific 4-1-0 start, and Shesterkin was a driving force behind that success. In just five appearances, Shesterkin posted 3.90 goals saved above average with a .900 high-danger save percentage, according to Natural Stat Trick.

    The 2022 Vezina Trophy winner, Shesterkin has put up sparkling numbers since he entered the NHL in 2019-20. In 330 games, Shesterkin boasts a .917 save percentage, a 2.51 GAA and 22 shutouts. Over the last three full seasons from 2023-26, Shesterkin ranked third in goals saved above average with 45.4. Only Connor Hellebuyck and Andrei Vasilevskiy were better in that category.

    Recent findings suggest that shesterkin was a big reason why the Rangers felt they could bounce back from a disappointing 2025-26 season, and losing the star goaltender puts a huge dent in the team's playoff hopes. It doesn't help that backup goalie Joonas Korpisalo is also hurt.

    In a recent development, dylan Garand replaced Shesterkin on Friday night, and Spencer Martin will be recalled from the AHL after recovering from his own injury. With the Rangers playing well early, it wouldn't be a shock to see them explore better replacement options for Shesterkin.

    Upcoming York won't be able to replace Shesterkin's impact because he's one of the five best goalies in the world. However, the team should be able to upgrade its current goaltending situation, which is a fairly low bar to clear.

    Recent findings suggest that first, there are unsigned veterans still on the open market in Petr Mrazek and James Reimer. Neither one was great last season -- hence their availability at the moment -- Reimer and Mrazek could provide a level of stability in the crease that the Rangers simply don't have right now.

    New York could also explore trade possibilities, and Minnesota Wild netminder Filip Gustavsson could be a solution there. Jesper Wallstedt is the future of the crease in Minnesota, making Gustavsson more of a luxury. Would the Wild send Gustavsson to New York in exchange for some draft capital it could use to acquire a center?

    It has been revealed that the one snag in a potential Gustavsson deal is his contract. Gustavsson is in the first year of a deal that pays him $6.8 million over the next five seasons. That's a significant commitment for a player who will become a backup when Shesterkin returns.

    Obviously, Connor Hellebuyck has been on the trade market for months now, but that trade wouldn't make sense for the Rangers. Hellebuyck is on an expensive long-term deal, and New York would have $20 million tied up in goalies if they made that move, not to mention the astronomical acquisition cost.

    Recent findings suggest that however, if you'll allow me to get creative here, it's no secret that the Florida Panthers have pursed Hellebuyck. What if the Panthers traded Jacob Markstrom -- just acquired in the offseason -- to the Rangers in order to make room for Hellebuyck?

    Markstrom does have a 20-team no-trade list, so the question is whether Newly introduced York would be one of his 11 approved teams. Florida flipping Markstrom so quickly seems like a long shot, but the team has taken plenty of substantial swings in recent history.

    Knicks' Mikal Bridges drills buzzer-beating 3-pointer to defeat Trail Blazers

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Fresh York Knicks are rounding into form, and maybe Saturday night is what Mikal Bridges needed to get back on track, too.
    • The 30-year-old wing, who came into a matchup with the Portland Trail Blazers shooting just north of 40% from the field and a smidge above 30% from deep, drilled a buzzer-beating 3-pointer to deliver Upcoming York a 97-96 victory in Madison Square Garden.
    • In a recent development, bridges finished with 12 points on 5-of-8 shooting.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Fresh York Knicks are rounding into form, and maybe Saturday night is what Mikal Bridges needed to get back on track, too.

    The 30-year-old wing, who came into a matchup with the Portland Trail Blazers shooting just north of 40% from the field and a smidge above 30% from deep, drilled a buzzer-beating 3-pointer to deliver Upcoming York a 97-96 victory in Madison Square Garden.

    In a recent development, bridges finished with 12 points on 5-of-8 shooting. He connected on two of his three attempts from long range. The last one extended the Knicks' win streak to four games.

    Sources indicate that following a pair of Deni Avdija free throws that put the Trail Blazers (10-6) up 96-94, Fresh York (10-6) took a timeout. With 3.2 seconds remaining, Josh Hart inbounded the ball to Bridges.

    He caught the pass to the right of the top of the arc, used a quick fake to get an overzealous Toumani Camara to bite, took one more dribble and introduced.

    In a recent development, the ball rattled in, the buzzer sounded and Mike Breen exclaimed, "Bang! Bang!".

    Bridges was swarmed by his Knicks teammates, eventually wearing a smile as MSG reveled in utter pandemonium.

    He came to the rescue on a night when New York squandered a 26-point lead. The Knicks shot 13 of 27 from 3-point land in the first half but scored only 31 points over the final two quarters.

    Bridges admitted afterward that Portland played "harder" than New York in the second half.

    Sources indicate that but he also noted in that on-court postgame interview: "It's 48 minutes. We just kept persevering through the time and ended up winning the game.".

    After trailing 94-84 with less than five minutes to go, the Trail Blazers went on a 12-0 run, which culminated in the aforementioned Avdija free throws. Additionally, that stretch featured a game-tying 3-pointer from Damian Lillard.

    Avdija was sent to the line because of a head-scratching foul by Knicks center Andre Drummond, who switched and committed the personal on the floor well beyond the arc.

    Industry observers note that avdija had 20 points. Center Donovan Clingan spearheaded Portland's effort with 22 points and 13 rebounds. Lillard put up just 15 points and shot a meager 1 of 9 from outside.

    Industry observers note that latest York was paced by Jalen Brunson's 30 points. Fellow guard Landry Shamet poured in 20 points.

    Bridges, though, was the hero, sinking a redemptive shot 16 games into what's been a trying season for the ninth-year pro.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Rumours of Manchester City’s supposed demise without Pep Guardiola appear to be much exaggerated.

    They swept past Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park with a style of play under fresh manager Enzo Maresca that was just as swashbuckling as under his predecessor, with Rayan Cherki playing the role of chief architect. The Frenchman’s two goals included a captivating mazy dribble, which will long be remembered by those who had the fortune to see it.

    Recent findings suggest that city created enough space for themselves through clever movement. With Cherki zigging one way and Phil Foden zagging the other, they created even more by dribbling past a mesmerised Palace back three that became a back five at times and still could not cope.

    Sources indicate that erling Haaland also scored twice. Even with the creative and unpredictable talents of those behind in a four-man attacking City midfield, Haaland remains irreplaceable with his ability to convert chances.

    However, this night belonged to Cherki. Guardiola chided him publicly after he set up a City goal with a “rabona” cross last season. The thrust of Guardiola’s comments were that Cherki was not Lionel Messi. Of course not, but he possesses a genius all of his own, which Maresca would surely be foolish to rein in.

    The jaw-dropping splendour of Cherki’s first goal drew a collective intake of breath at Selhurst Park.

    Collecting a Foden pass, he attacked the Palace area on a diagonal path, slaloming between Jaydee Canvot, Takehiro Tomiyasu and Chris Richards, before having the spatial awareness and technique to flick his left foot at the ball to send it rolling on a perpendicular trajectory past Dean Henderson.

    "The man with the magic feet!"Rayan Cherki doubles Manchester City's lead with a STUNNING goal 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/9Zea5vFljv.

    An insight into Cherki’s mindset came after the match.

    He remarked: “My performance is s---. In the first half, we didn’t find the space, I played bad. I need to show them that I want to play, I want to score. Next time I want to give the ball around more.”.

    Forget the words, Maresca cannot ignore the actions of a player he left on the bench against Bournemouth.

    Sterner tests will come for City than against a Palace side missing key players who may or may not leave south London in the remaining days of the transfer window.

    Whether Maresca will trust his forward players to express themselves as freely against their rivals for the Premier League title remains to be seen, but with Elliot Anderson providing a one-man shield behind them, City could not be stopped.

    Maresca said: “For sure Rayan is happy tonight. His performance was very good and not just for his two goals. He has to press off the ball and he was in charge of [marking] Adam Wharton, so it was a complete game by him.”.

    Only for the first three minutes did Palace hint at a different outcome but, after shots from Eddie Nketiah and Daichi Kamada were diverted away for corners, City took control.

    They took the lead in the 17th minute when the otherwise quiet Antoine Semenyo flighted a cross over the heads of everyone except the shorn locks of Haaland, whose determined header looped over Henderson and dropped in the far corner.

    The only negative of Foden’s performance came in front of goal, with a ballooned shot and a mistimed header.

    After Cherki’s solo masterpiece had made it 2-0, Yeremy Pino seized the next moment for his own with a stunning free-kick that flicked the crossbar, then the back of City keeper Gianluigi Donnarumma before finally dropping over the line.

    "This is a good a free-kick as you're likely to see this season!" Yéremy Pino's stirke beats Donnarumma 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5uF4vzOXDp.

    Whatever hope that mustered was snatched away again when Cherki scored his second goal and the third goal of a breathless five minutes.

    His shot at the end of a darting run flicked the ankle of Tomiyasu to send it just out of Henderson’s reach.

    It has been revealed that rayan Cherki AGAIN! Manchester City have breathing room once again after another strike from the Frenchman 👏 pic.twitter.com/Tyw9whPS2r.

    Morocco teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi had little time to show why City have paid Lille £85.6m for him with a late entry as a substitute, but they didn’t need him on this occasion.

    Foden then set off on a swerving run that set up Haaland to lash home his second goal of the game and make it 4-1.

    Erling Haaland scores gets another! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/4mz2eF7wFF.

    The fear for Palace is that they cannot keep selling their best players and expecting to replicate the success on the pitch that has brought them three trophies in the past 15 months.

    Industry observers note that leicester City offer a shuddering example of that. From Premier League champions to League One in 10 seasons.

    Pierre Sage, the new Palace manager, will welcome the certainty that the closure of the transfer window will bring, particularly over the futures of forwards Ismaïla Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta, as well as wing-back Daniel Muñoz.

    The one player he cannot afford to lose is Wharton, who matched the City midfield on his own at times in the first half.

    Sage said: “I think the score is heavy. We stayed in the game for 65 minutes and created some chances. We know we are in for a tough season, but we have created a lot of opportunities in the first two games.

    According to recent reports, “I could speak about the transfer window, but I don’t want to find an excuse. We just have to be sure that in four days’ time, the team will be better than today.”.

    “It has been a short pre-season. Rayan [Cherki], five weeks ago was at the World Cup. Game by game, we will be back, just need a few games. We played well, it is a upcoming manager but we have been playing together, with the addition of a few new players. We know what to do and have to trust the system.”.

    In a recent development, “We have to keep on playing together, find out where we are best and how to play. We have so many good players and we have to fit everyone in. He has to keep going because we know how good Phil is, it is about showing it week in week out. This is the right step forward for everyone. We have to build on this.”.

    Manchester City: Donnarumma, Khusanov, Dias, Gvardiol, O’Reilly, Anderson, Guehi, Cherki, Foden Semenyo, Haaland.Substitutes: Rulli, Kovacic, Ait-Nouri, Reis, Echeverri, Bouaddi, McAidoo, Braithwaite, Lewis.

    Sources indicate that was it really just a year ago when Crystal Palace fans flooded down the Holmesdale Road with not a care in the world having just won the Community Shield to add to their FA Cup triumph over tonight’s opponents Manchester City? Well, they are marching along the Holmesdale Road in the same numbers again this evening, bedecked in red and blue as always, yet there is uncertainty and worry in the air and on their faces. Will the player exodus continue? What should they make of new manager Pierre Sage? Will the good times fade from view as swiftly as they did for Leicester City or can Sage build a new side to match the one which, under Oliver Glasner, added the Conference League to their list of trophies three months ago?

    “We struggled to get into the game and win the battles,” a disappointed Carlo Ancelotti lamented.

    Sources indicate that at the World Cup, an industrious 18-year-old showed maturity beyond his years to dominate the midfield against Ancelotti’s Brazil on his competitive international debut, earning Morocco a draw. That was, in fact, the second time an Ancelotti side had been undone by precocious teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi.

    Ancelotti’s remarks about losing the midfield battle are from after a Champions League match in October 2024, when Lille shocked Real Madrid to end their 36-game unbeaten run. Bouaddi was at the heart of both statement results for his club and country.

    Tonight:Crystal Palace vs Manchester City.

    Saturday:Liverpool vs Nottingham ForestBournemouth vs EvertonCoventry vs Hull CityTottenham vs Newcastle.

    Sunday:Chelsea vs BrightonLeeds vs BrentfordSunderland vs FulhamManchester United vs Ipswich.

    Industry observers note that COYP. 🦅 pic.twitter.com/78ZUj8SBOf.

    The second weekend of the Premier League season kicks off under the lights in South London as Crystal Palace host Manchester City at Selhurst Park. Manchester City won both fixtures 3-0 last season and they are in fact unbeaten in their last 11 Premier league away games against Crystal Palace, who have won just two of the 22 top flight meetings.

    According to recent reports, crystal Palace experienced defeat on the opening weekend, falling to a 2-0 loss at Everton last Saturday, meaning the Pierre Sage era started with a defeat. Tonight is Sage’s first home game in charge of the club.

    “I think it will be a wonderful moment, but I prefer to have a wonderful moment with good news at the end of the game,” Sage mentioned. “That is why I do not think about me in this situation. The most important thing is the team and the result for sure, because we prepare all the week for that, to make them [the fans] happy. They will be happy to see us, but I think they would prefer to see us win. I will give my life to make them happy. I cannot do more. When you are in this stadium [Selhurst Park], you feel the history. You feel that there is something heavy weighing on you. It is a great responsibility that I have been entrusted with. We cannot wait to see this stadium in action.”.

    Sage has confirmed that Ismaila Sarr, who has been linked with a move away from the club this summer, and Chadi Riad will miss out tonight due to injury, as will striker Jean-Philippe Mateta. Palace have confirmed the addition of Axel Disasi on loan from Chelsea and the French defender could be involved tonight.

    Industry observers note that manchester City appeared to be heading towards defeat in Enzo Maresca’s first league game in charge of the club last weekend. They were 1-0 down at home against Bournemouth in the closing stages before goals from Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol gave them a come-from-behind win.

    Sources indicate that it has been a busy week in the transfer window for Manchester City. Both Savio (formerly Savinho) and Omar Marmoush have left for Tottenham, joining a long list of departures from the Etihad this summer. Moroccan midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi has arrived in an £85m deal from Lille and has become the most expensive teenager in Premier League history. Maresca has confirmed that 18-year-old Bouaddi is ready to start.

    “He [Bouaddi] is ready,” Maresca noted. “He was working with his former club so he is fit. We will see how long he needs in terms of adaptation but he is ready to go. He is quite calm. He does not look 18, he already looks older, which is crucial. But in this case, we need to go slowly because he is very young, he has come from a different country so there is no rush for him. He is going to help us now and in the future. He is very mature for being 18.”.

    Team news from Selhurst Park to follow shortly.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Hungary manager Marco Rossi has defended his usage of Dominik Szoboszlai during this international window.
    • The Liverpool midfielder sprained his knee during the Reds’ 3-1 victory at Crystal Palace the weekend before last and admitted that he nearly pulled out of his country’s win over Georgia six days later.
    • His choice to represent his nation was condemned by some reporters back on Merseyside, amid fears of aggravating the injury and compromising his involvement for his club over the coming weeks as the fixtures come thick and fast for Andoni Iraola’s side.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Hungary manager Marco Rossi has defended his usage of Dominik Szoboszlai during this international window.

    The Liverpool midfielder sprained his knee during the Reds’ 3-1 victory at Crystal Palace the weekend before last and admitted that he nearly pulled out of his country’s win over Georgia six days later.

    His choice to represent his nation was condemned by some reporters back on Merseyside, amid fears of aggravating the injury and compromising his involvement for his club over the coming weeks as the fixtures come thick and fast for Andoni Iraola’s side.

    Rossi was defiant when quizzed about Szoboszlai ahead of Hungary’s match against Northern Ireland on Tuesday night.

    He told reporters (via Origo Sport): “Did you see any problems with Dominik in the Georgia game? Because I didn’t see any. He played like he usually does, so there are no problems from our side. He claims he’s ready, he’s available, so he’ll play.”.

    The Hungary boss was true to his word, as the Liverpool star played the entirety of the Northern Ireland game, thankfully seeming to come through it without any adverse effects.

    Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

    We can understand Szoboszlai wanting to represent his country, especially in his role as captain, but those who pay his wages at Anfield mightn’t have been overly impressed with his decision to play on despite knowing prior to the Georgia match that he wasn’t operating at 100%.

    That Liverpool don’t play until Sunday at 4:30pm gives the 26-year-old that bit of additional time to manage his fitness carefully so that he’s in prime condition for the game against Manchester United.

    Whether or not the midfielder will start that match is debatable. The in-form Alexis Mac Allister and Florian Wirtz will likely have two of the three midfield berths nailed down, and the excellent displays of Trey Nyoni have made it difficult to omit him from the XI.

    Also, if Iraola feels that Szoboszlai isn’t fully fit by Sunday, he probably won’t take the risk of throwing our number 8 back into the starting line-up, instead keeping him in reserve should he be needed off the bench.

    Hopefully the influential Hungarian won’t suffer any further complications over the next four days, and everyone associated with Liverpool will surely be glad that the international window is out of the way, with the next one not upon us until late March 2027.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    One of the biggest benefits of the NIL era is that college basketball has more elite talent than ever, now that players are returning for bigger paychecks instead of bolting for NBA money at the first opportunity.

    That made selecting our 2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America teams especially difficult, but our experts nailed it. Each of the three teams features players who will be performing at the next level very soon, but the best of those might be Florida superstar Thomas Haugh.

    As our own Isaac Trotter explains, if Haugh can improve his range shooting, he won't have to wait long to hear his name called in the 2027 NBA Draft.

    When it comes to how the talent broke down by conference, it was a a pretty level playing field for the most part.

    Not to spoil anyting, but Arizona freshman Caleb Holt did not make the cut. He did, however, turn some heads in the Wildcats' exhibition game.

    Recent findings suggest that loyalty is an excellent quality to have in a friend or partner. It's also why we love dogs.

    It should not be quite as prevalent among college football coaches, some of whom have been undone because they did what was comfortable, not what was necessarily best for the team.

    Our own John Talty highlighted five high-profile coaches who have been loyal to a fault, making hires and personnel decisions that have come back to haunt them. One of those coaches is Mike Elko. After a shaky season from Marcel Reed in 2025, Texas A&M chose not to pursue an upgrade in the portal.

    Instead, the Aggies gave Reed a major payday, and they'll miss the College Football Playoff because of it.

    Look, it can happen to the best of us. Dan Lanning and Dabo Swinney wound up on the list, despite the success that those two have had throughout their careers.

    Industry observers note that steve Sarkisian is another coach who has fallen into the trap of being too loyal, but he may have a huge decision on his hands in the offseason. Arch Manning has struggled enough that another year in college should be on the table. If that happens, would Sark welcome back Manning with open arms, despite his shortcomings?

    Finally, one person for whom loyalty is no an problem is Missouri QB Austin Simmons. After Trinidad Chambliss won the starting job at Ole Miss last year, Simmons didn't feel the need to stick around, but there won't be bitterness when Simmons returns to Oxford this weekend.

    • By game's end, Wembanyama had scored 50 points, his second 50-point performance of the season, this time in a 114-91 victory over the Pelicans (5-13) at Frost Bank Center.
    • It has been revealed that the 7-foot-4 superstar went for 52 points in a Nov.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Victor Wembanyama outscored the New Orleans Pelicans' starters in the first half on Saturday night at home. He had 32 points. They had 26.

    By game's end, Wembanyama had scored 50 points, his second 50-point performance of the season, this time in a 114-91 victory over the Pelicans (5-13) at Frost Bank Center.

    It has been revealed that the 7-foot-4 superstar went for 52 points in a Nov. 4 win over the Dallas Mavericks. Both of those outings have coincided with San Antonio (14-3) going 14-1 following an 0-2 start.

    Wembanyama, still only 22, has already tied Spurs legend David Robinson for the second-most 50-plus-point games in franchise history with three. George Gervin, a Basketball Hall of Famer like Robinson, leads the way with five.

    It has been revealed that wembanyama's got a long runway to surpass both Robinson and Gervin in that department. A third 50-piece this season would be historic in itself.

    He's the third player since 1973-74 to log at least 50 points, 15 rebounds and 5 blocks in a single game. Wembanyama clocked out after shooting 20 of 29 with 18 rebounds, 5 blocks and 4 steals.

    "It is very special," Wembanyama said, when asked about reaching the 50-point threshold in an on-court postgame interview.

    He then remarked with a smile: "But unlike many of my peers, I'm not very good at stat padding. So I haven't reached it as many times as I should have.".

    Actress Selena Gomez was sitting courtside at the game. Wembanyama noticed.

    "Of course, I had to show off for Selena, you know," he said, laughing.

    The Spurs pulled away in the second quarter. San Antonio also got 19 points from guard Stephon Castle. Another backcourt contributor, De'Aaron Fox, piled up 10 assists.

    In a recent development, the Pelicans are 1-9 in their last 10 games. They've come undone after beginning the 2026-27 campaign with a 4-4 record. A bright spot for Newly introduced Orleans is the continued growth of 20-year-old guard Jeremiah Fears, who led the team with 29 points in the loss.

    As for Wembanyama, he's once again an NBA MVP candidate. It's looking like he'll face stiff competition for that award this season as well.

    Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Dončić has a pair of 50-point games under his belt, too, and he's leading the league in scoring with 37.2 points per contest.

    • Andoni Iraola wanted to talk about his team and their need to improve but how could he concentrate on something so straightforward when he had seen something so bizarre?

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Andoni Iraola wanted to talk about his team and their need to improve but how could he concentrate on something so straightforward when he had seen something so bizarre?

    According to recent reports, it is important, first and foremost, to explain this is not painting a narrative about Liverpool being unfortunate. Far from it. Iraola hissed his dismay that Nottingham Forest had shown more intensity and been the better team for long periods in an entertaining 2-2 draw.

    Recent findings suggest that but the penalty that changed the contest? Iraola, his coaching staff, even the supporters behind the dugout had been left flabbergasted that the malfunctioning number board of fourth official Tim Robinson presented an avenue for Forest to exploit.

    Iraola had tried to make a triple change, wanting to introduce Ryan Gravenberch, Kostas Tsimikas and Rio Ngumoha, but as Robinson pressed buttons to no avail and everyone in Red became frustrated, Forest substitute Liam Delap took a quick throw and the Liverpool house almost caved in.

    According to recent reports, neco Williams, once of Liverpool, surged into the penalty area, Alisson Becker arrived a fraction too late after the defender got his shot away and took his old team-mate down. Morgan Gibbs-White exacerbated the damage when sending Alisson the wrong way and this was the last thing a manager wanting to make an impression on a significant day needed to see but this was reality.

    Alisson takes out Neco Williams and Forest have a penalty! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fX2flY3Tob.

    According to recent reports, gibbs-White converts from the spot to restore Forest's lead! 🌳🎯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/jeoPiXPArw.

    “I cannot explain because I don’t have an explanation,” Iraola noted. “I wanted to make those substitutions about three minutes before. I mean, it was two, three, four times the ball had gone out. I still don’t know the reason why we couldn’t make the subs.

    Sources indicate that “I think [the fourth official] was having some problems with the board or something. It [the penalty] wouldn’t have happened if I had made the sub. I asked. I had complained the previous time. The supporters were shouting and they were aware of the situation. But I don’t know what happened and I don’t know why they have given the penalty.”.

    "A professional fourth official cannot take three minutes." 😳Andoni Iraola was not happy with the time taken to get the substitutes' board ready.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fMfYOjQJPd.

    He did know, though, why Liverpool had needed to drag themselves off the deck again for the second week in a row. Iraola has shown in his opening weeks on Merseyside that he is not someone who seeks excuses.

    “A lack of intensity hurt us,” Iraola said with obvious disdain and it was only down to a show of character in the second period that a slovenly first half did not enable Forest to win at Anfield for the third consecutive year, for all that the travelling fans thought it was “happening again!”.

    Forest, bruised after two defeats in four days to Leeds, looked like an Oliver Glasner side. They were aggressive and well organised, the only failing was that physically they could not see the job through, but the Austrian insisted that will change in due course.

    Once Glasner is settled in and he gets his transfer business done – “definitely one, possibly two and probably three,” was his mischievous reply to how the window will unfold – Forest will be a formidable proposition, especially if the first 45 minutes are a barometer.

    They had been knocking on the door before Dan Ndoye eventually broke the deadlock, sweeping a left-footed drive past Alisson after Igor Jesus had won a header from a long clearance. It was a simple goal, marginally onside, but it was absolutely deserved.

    Industry observers note that ndoye gives Forest the lead at Anfield! 🌳🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ag0oZ7UjTm.

    Recent findings suggest that “There were many positive aspects,” said Glasner. “It has been a three-game week; some players played. We are getting more and more fitness, that is just the foundation of how we want to play. It is just a point but it still feels a bit frustrating, so we have to stay humble.”.

    "I think we were very poor in the first half." 😤Andoni Iraola gives his assessment of Liverpool's performance against Nottingham Forest.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/COZfhwkLeX.

    Neco Williams and James McAtee react to Nottingham Forest's draw at Anfield 🌳🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BjX0p1yQ1m.

    The playmaker added another goal and assist to his tally this afternoon.

    Liverpool and Forest are both made to wait for their first Premier League wins of the season as the two sides play out a pulsating 2-2 draw at Anfield.

    Full-time scenes at Anfield as Liverpool and Nottingham Forest share the points 🤝📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/WqOpfU38es.

    Sels calmly comes out to claim a deep cross to relieve the pressure on Forest. Munoz runs back to dispossess Delap and win a free kick, giving Liverpool another chance to launch the ball forward.

    Glasner makes a very late double change as Hudson-Odoi and Dominguez replace McAtee and Igor Jesus.

    It has been revealed that there will be five minutes of added time. Liverpool continue their relentless search for a third goal, while Forest are holding on.

    It’s wave after wave of Liverpool pressure. Forest are camped inside their own half. Igor Jesus and Delap are chasing every loose ball, but Forest are struggling to get out at the moment.

    Recent findings suggest that munoz’s goal has provided another twist in this pulsating encounter. Isak wins a free kick in such dangerous territory and Szoboszlai steps up to take it. The Hungarian slams a venomous effort wide of the far post. Can either side find a late winner?

    What an incredible finish! Wirtz threads a delightful pass through to Munoz. With his back to goal, the winger swivels and takes the ball on the outside of Murillo, before smashing a thunderous effort into the roof of the net, which brushes the crossbar on its way in.

    Munoz, take a bow! 🤯👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/GD8IAdy2rJ.

    Igor Jesus does brilliantly to escape Nyoni, before he is pulled to the ground by Arajou, who is booked. It’s been an excellent defensive effort from Forest.

    Iraola makes his final two alterations as Araujo and Nyoni replace Jacquet and Mac Allister. Szoboszlai then swings such an inviting delivery into the penalty area, but Isak miscues his strike with his left foot.

    Amid the chaos, Alisson was booked just before the penalty after appealing the decision and Iraola has ordered a triple change, taking off Kerkez, Frimpong and Gakpo for Tsimikas, Gravenberch and Ngumoha. This has seen Szoboszlai move out to right back.

    Andoni Iraola is about to make his substitution and this is interesting because he had planned to introduce Rio Ngumoha, Kostas Tsimikas and Ryan Gravenberch 10 minutes ago but told them to sit down after Liverpool had equalised. Forest have put Liam Delap on, giving him his debut after completing his £45m move to the club.

    The Forest captain sends Alisson the wrong way, powering a clinical penalty into the net. Gibbs-White demonstrates fantastic composure and Liverpool have it all to do again.

    Gibbs-White converts from the spot to restore Forest's lead! 🌳🎯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/jeoPiXPArw.

    Delap showcases excellent initiative and takes a quick throw-in to send Williams through on goal. Alisson rushes out and catches Williams as he attempts to lob the goalkeeper. Williams crashes to the ground and the referee points to the spot. Alisson is furious. What a chance for Forest to restore their lead.

    Alisson takes out Neco Williams and Forest have a penalty! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fX2flY3Tob.

    It has been revealed that this game is being played at a ferocious pace and Forest’s club-record signing Delap enters the action as he replaces Ndoye. Can the former Chelsea striker mark his debut with a much-needed goal?

    That leveller has injected so much energy into Liverpool. Anfield believes again. Isak really needed that goal.

    So much credit must go to Gakpo. The winger shrugs off Williams and fires a pinpoint cross towards the back post. Isak is there and converts from close range. We’re set up for such an intriguing finale. Liverpool have the momentum now.

    According to recent reports, isak equalises for Liverpool at the Kop end! 🔴🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/qKFxq2AqaB.

    Wirtz’s frustrating afternoon is compounded as he picks up a booking after hauling Murillo to the ground. Iraola looks to be readying some substitutions.

    There is a very strange feeling here: it’s almost a case of the home fans waiting for Nottingham Forest to score a second goal rather than anticipating that Liverpool will equalise. The early buzz in the atmosphere has gone and that is because the gaps everyone can see in the make up of the team remain. How Bradley Barcola will transform this situation?

    Jacquet’s pass is intercepted and Ndoye is released on the counter. He’s guided out wide by Van Dijk but still squeezes in a brilliant cross. Gibbs-White was running up the pitch in support and slowed down, meaning no one was there to turn in Ndoye’s delivery.

    Munoz is the next player to be booked after reacting angrily to a decision. Iraola has to consider making some changes soon.

    Aina catches Munoz with a late challenge and he’s the second Forest player to go into the referee’s book.

    Industry observers note that you can already see in this second half that there is acres of space for Forest to exploit on the counter as Liverpool push for a leveller. Munoz then heads a point-blank header over the bar. Luckily for the Spaniard, the offside flag was up against Gakpo.

    We are back for the second half here at Anfield. Can Liverpool find a route back into this game or can Forest hold onto the three points?

    It’s a bizarre situation for Liverpool. They could easily be level or be 2-0 down. But they trial just 1-0 at half-time. Wirtz and Gakpo are looking lively, but Isak has struggled to influence the game.

    Dan Ndoye scores his first goal in the Premier League in 377 days 🤯 pic.twitter.com/tjSiGoSPyW.

    Recent findings suggest that forest have a slender one-goal advantage at the break after a frantic first half at Anfield. Ndoye curled the visitors into a well-deserved lead after 24 minutes, before Wirtz had a goal ruled out for offside. The German was then sensationally denied by Sels’ diving save as he tipped Wirtz’s header over the bar. Alisson then replicated Sels’ heroics, parrying Igor Jesus’ strike against the woodwork to stop Forest from doubling their lead.

    What a move and what a save! Murillo sprays an inch-perfect pass out to Aina, who chops inside of Munoz and fires a low cross into Igor Jesus. The Forest striker shoots first-time from inside the penalty area, but his effort is sensationally parried onto the bar by Alisson. That is a world-class stop from the Brazilian goalkeeper.

    Igor Jesus receives the game’s first yellow card after clipping Mac Allister with an unnecessary challenge.

    Liverpool then fly forward again as Gakpo nutmegs Williams. His cross trickles through to Munoz at the back post. The ball is slightly behind Munoz and he leans back before shooting, causing his strike to narrowly sail over the bar.

    There will be three minutes of added time to conclude this first half.

    It has been revealed that liverpool are applying all the pressure at the end of this first half. At times, Forest have had every outfield player behind the ball.

    Sels makes a superb save! Gakpo takes on his marker on the outside and fires in a cross which Wirtz meets. The attacker gets in between Schlager and Aina to win the header, but his effort is excellently tipped over the bar by Sels.

    In a recent development, out of nothing, Liverpool are level. McAtee attempts to play out from a deep position and his pass is intercepted by Wirtz. The ball breaks to Frimpong, who slips a clever pass to Wirtz. The German playmaker swivels and slides a low effort into the bottom corner. It’s a brilliant finish, but Frimpong was in an offside position before he provided the assist. VAR confirms this and Liverpool’s joy has been cut short. That is a huge let off for Forest, who need to be more careful with possession in deeper areas.

    Following that Forest goal, there was a small flurry of Liverpool pressure, with Szoboszlai having a free kick punched away by Sels. Murillo is then very careless with the ball and is dispossessed. This allowed Mac Allister to play in Isak, but the striker is crowded out by multiple Forest defenders before he can get a shot away.

The Forest captain plays in Ndoye and the winger curls a clinical effort into the far bottom corner to send the away support wild.

    Back home ❤️ pic.twitter.com/tJJBqD4Sfj.

    Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League match between Liverpool and Nottingham Forest at Anfield.

    This encounter pits two summer appointments – Andoni Iraola and Oliver Glasner – against each other as they both search for their first top-flight win at their upcoming clubs.

    It has been revealed that in the opening Premier League game-week, Iraola’s Liverpool needed a last-gasp 99th-minute penalty from Dominik Szoboszlai to rescue an unconvincing 2-2 draw with Newcastle United at St. James’ Park. Meanwhile, Nottingham Forest have suffered back-to-back home defeats in four days against Leeds United without scoring (1-0 Premier League, 2-0 Carabao Cup).

    Iraola has been handed the unenviable task of steering Liverpool back on track following a hugely disappointing campaign under Arne Slot, whose side’s defence of their Premier League ended in a meek fifth-place finish despite spending more than £400m in the previous summer.

    The former Bournemouth boss must uncover how to get the best out of massive-money recruits such as Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Milos Kerkez and Jeremie Frimpong, and also tighten up Liverpool’s vulnerable midfield and defence. Given the pressure of the job and the club’s hectic schedule while balancing domestic and European football, it’s a tough ask. However, Liverpool have agreed a £120m deal for Paris St-Germain winger Bradley Barcola to bolster their attacking reinforcements, but the transfer hasn’t been finalised in time for today’s match.

    Last season, Forest endured an equally tumultuous campaign, churning through a staggering four managers, before eventually stumbling to a 16th-place finish. Glasner has been hand-picked by owner Evangelos Marinakis to usher in an era of stability and success, after winning the FA Cup, Community Shield and Conference League in just over two years at Crystal Palace.

    Industry observers note that both Marinakis and Glasner are extremely ambitious and demanding figures. You’d imagine a top-half finish would be considered the absolute minimum for Forest, while Glasner’s track record of winning trophies surely indicates that Marinakis is eyeing some silverware at the City Ground.

    Sources indicate that it’s a meeting of two managers who must deliver. Three points for either side would serve as a much-needed tonic to kickstart their seasons.

    Kick-off is at 12:30, with team news coming shortly.

    Tech Report: Connor Hellebuyck trade: Jets send star goalie to the Devils in exchange for four players, two draft picks

    📅 24 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1151 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The star goalie for the Winnipeg Jets is on the move after being traded to Upcoming Jersey on Friday in exchange for four players and two future draft picks.
    • Hellebuyck expressed his desire to be traded in the offseason when he formally requested a move in August.
    • According to recent reports, hellebuyck has spent his entire career with Winnipeg after being drafted by the Jets in 2012 at No.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Connor Hellebuyck is a now a Devil. The star goalie for the Winnipeg Jets is on the move after being traded to Upcoming Jersey on Friday in exchange for four players and two future draft picks. the teams declared the move with the Jets receiving Dawson Mercer, Nick Bjugstad, Nico Daws and Alexander Command, plus a 2027 seventh-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick.

    Hellebuyck expressed his desire to be traded in the offseason when he formally requested a move in August. He mentioned at the time that he had made the request months earlier and tried to keep the situation private.

    According to recent reports, hellebuyck has spent his entire career with Winnipeg after being drafted by the Jets in 2012 at No. 130 overall. He's recognized as one of the best goalies in the league as a three-time Vezina Trophy winner. He also helped carry the United States to its first gold medal since 1980 at the 2026 Olympics in February with some incredible saves against Canada in the final game.

    After trading Jacob Markstom in the offseason, the Devils had a clear need in goal, and this splashy move certainly fills that need. With a talented young core already in place, Latest Jersey's Stanley Cup window is wide open.

    RAISE HELLE!Connor Hellebuyck is a Latest Jersey Devil: https://t.co/HCehRGOQI5 pic.twitter.com/dZGNQR16m1.

    For the Jets, it must be a hard pill to swallow when a franchise icon decides to walk out they door, but this trade package should help them as the enter a fresh era and revamp the roster. Winnipeg got a former first-rounder in Mercer to try and add to a rebuild as well as a veteran presence in Bjugstad. They also acquired a younger goalie in Daws who could fill the role of Hellebuyck at just 25 years old.

    Recent findings suggest that goaltending has been an issue in New Jersey for a while now -- even after the team acquired Markstrom from the Calgary Flames in 2024. Markstom never really panned out, and his 13.6 goals allowed above average, per Natural Stat Trick, were a substantial reason why the Devils missed the postseason last year.

    In a recent development, in the early portion of this season, it was clear that New Jersey needed to make a move to upgrade in the crease. Daws and veteran Jake Allen simply aren't a tandem suitable for a Stanley Cup contender, and the numbers backed that up. New Jersey ranks 24th in team save percentage at .877, and the duo of Daws and Allen combined to surrender 2.99 goals above average.

    Once Hellebuyck gets up to game speed, that shouldn't be a problem anymore.

    In the three-season stretch from 2023-26, Hellebuyck led the NHL with 73.42 goals saved above average, which is 20 goals higher than the next closest netminder. Over that span, Hellebuyck also posted a standard save percentage of .914 and an astronomical high-danger save-percentage of .832.

    Recent findings suggest that hellebuyck carried less talented teams to the playoffs multiple times in his career. Now on a team loaded with weaponry in their prime -- Jack Hughes, Jesper Bratt and Nico Hischier to name a few -- Hellebuyck could be the final piece to the championship puzzle.

    Sources indicate that in terms of the acquisition cost, it was probably an easy deal for Devils general manager Sunny Mehta to make. The 2029 second-round pick is useless for a team that should be all-in now, Bjugstad is simply a depth piece and Daws now has no path to a starting role with Hellebuyck in town.

    Industry observers note that the most interesting trade chips are Mercer and Command. Mercer flashed major upside with 56 points in his second NHL season, 2022-23, but he hasn't really come close to hitting those heights again. Still, even if he has plateaued, Mercer remains a strong middle-six forward rising into his prime.

    According to recent reports, although Command had his detractors -- and may have been over-drafted at No. 12 overall -- he was a consensus first-round pick last summer. That gives Winnipeg a potential franchise forward it can build around long-term, but Fresh Jersey already has one of the deepest forward groups in the league, especially with the emergence of Arseny Gritsyuk and the acquisition of Luke Evangelista.

    If we're looking for a 3-D chess angle of this deal, it only makes the Devils more appealing for a certain Minnesota Wild defenseman whose brothers just happen to play in Latest Jersey already. Grade -- A+.

    Sources indicate that let's get the obvious out of the way first: The Jets were never going to get fair value for Hellebuyck because, at his best, he's the No. 1 goaltender in the world with no equal. That type of excellence can't be replaced.

    Recent findings suggest that that mentioned, Winnipeg did fairly well given the circumstances. Hellebuyck made a public trade request, and he wasn't even with the team after sitting out for the entirety of training camp. The entire league knew the Jets had to trade him.

    Hellebuyck's talent created a decent market anyway, but most of the suitors were bona fide Stanley Cup contenders with little in the way of valuable draft capital, and they weren't going to knee cap the roster by sending a key player back in return.

    With all that taken into consideration, Kevin Cheveldayoff got a solid return. Although Mercer's ceiling may be lower than initially thought, he's a 24-year-old forward who banks roughly 20 goals and 20 assists every season. The kicker with Mercer will be Winnipeg's ability to re-sign him before he hits restricted free agency next summer.

    Recent findings suggest that the addition of Command means Winnipeg now has two forwards selected in the top 12 of the 2026 NHL Draft after taking center Viggo Bjorck themselves. If both of those players deliver on their first-round pedigrees, they could be a terrific one-two punch for the team long-term.

    In a recent development, daws was a third-round pick in 2020, and despite playing just 13 NHL games since the start of the 2024-25 season, he should give Winnipeg a solid back up option behind Stuart Skinner. It certainly helps that Skinner is off to a great start with his newly introduced team -- and if Daws develops into a true No. 1 -- it'll be gravy.

    If there's any reason to critique this deal from the Jets' side of things, it's that they didn't get premium draft capital or a surefire up-and-coming prospect. Maybe Command develops into a star, but there's no guarantee he becomes a top-six stud in the NHL.

    Recent findings suggest that the Jets got a lot of good stuff, but they didn't really get anything great, at least not based on what we know in the moment. Because of that, I have to ding Winnipeg a little bit. Grade: B.
